claims.statement: The púca (Irish; púcaí), also pwca, pooka, phouka, puck, is a creature of Celtic, English and Channel Islands folklore, bringing good and bad fortune.
claims.statement_id: Púca (Irlandia, Irish; púcaí), juga pwca, pooka, phouka, puck, makhluk cerita rakyat Kelt (Celtic), Inggris (English), Kepulauan Channel (Channel Islands); pembawa untung dan sial; di Irlandia dan Britania.
claims.quote: (Irish for spirit/ghost; plural púcaí), puca (Old English for goblin), also pwca, pooka, pookah, phouka, and puck, is a creature of Celtic, English, and Channel Islands folklore. Considered to be bringers both of good and bad fortune, they could help or hinder rural and marine communities.

claims.statement: Púcaí have dark or white fur and shift into horses, goats, cats, dogs, hares, or humans with animal ears or tails.
claims.statement_id: Púcaí berbulu gelap atau putih, berubah menjadi kuda, kambing, kucing, anjing, kelinci, atau menyamar manusia bertelinga atau berekor hewan.
claims.quote: Púcaí can have dark or white fur or hair. The creatures were said to be shape-changers that could take the appearance of horses, goats, cats, dogs, and hares. They may also take a human disguise, which includes various animal features, such as animal ears or a tail.

claims.statement: The Irish word púca comes from Middle English puck; Welsh pwca, Cornish bucca.
claims.statement_id: Kata Irlandia púca dari Inggris Pertengahan (Middle English) puck; dalam mitologi Wales (Welsh) pwca, Cornwall (Cornish) bucca.
claims.quote: The Irish word púca is of English origin, the etymon being Middle English puck. The púca has counterparts throughout the Celtic and Germanic cultures of Northwest Europe.

claims.statement: Per Thomas Keightley, a boy near Killarney said pookas were wicked black things coming as wild colts with chains, harming travellers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Thomas Keightley, anak dekat Killarney bercerita púca jahat dan hitam, muncul sebagai anak kuda liar berantai, mencelakai pelancong.
claims.quote: were wicked-minded, black-looking, bad things ... that would come in the form of wild colts, with chains hanging about them", and that did much to harm unwary travellers.

claims.statement: The púca entices people to ride on its back for a wild journey, then drops them back where they started.
claims.statement_id: Púca membujuk manusia menunggang punggungnya untuk perjalanan liar lalu menjatuhkannya di tempat semula.
claims.quote: They are commonly said to entice humans to take a ride on their back, giving the rider a wild and terrifying journey before dropping the unlucky person back at the place they were taken from.

claims.statement: Its preferred form is a black pony (schwarzen Ponys).
claims.statement_id: Wujud kesukaannya kuda poni hitam (schwarzen Ponys).
claims.quote: Die bevorzugte Erscheinungsform ist die eines schwarzen Ponys.

claims.statement: Grain left in fields after Samhain belongs to the púcas; per Ó Súilleabháin, Halloween is called Púca night. (Ireland)
claims.statement_id: Biji-bijian di ladang setelah Samhain milik púca; menurut Ó Súilleabháin, Halloween disebut Púca night; di Irlandia (Irland). (Ireland)
claims.quote: Bei der Ernteeinbringung ist alles, was nach Samhain auf den Feldern an Getreideähren zurückbleibt, Eigentum der Púcas. Nach Ó Súilleabháin wird Halloween auch „Púca night“ genannt.

claims.statement: The púca usually throws its guest off a cliff or into a bog and vanishes laughing.
claims.statement_id: Púca biasanya menjatuhkan tamunya ke jurang atau rawa lalu menghilang sambil tertawa.
claims.quote: Meist wirft Púca seinen „Gast“ dann eine Klippe runter oder ins Moor und verschwindet unter schallendem Gelächter.

claims.statement: In English folklore, the Puck (Goodfellows) are demons or fairies, domestic or nature sprites.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Puck (Goodfellows) demon atau peri, roh rumah atau roh alam; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: In English folklore, The Puck (/ˈpʌk/), also known as Goodfellows, are demons or fairies which can be domestic sprites or nature sprites.

claims.statement: Attested in Old English as puca; similar to Old Norse púki and Celtic Welsh pwca, Cornish bucca, Irish púca. (Scandinavian)
claims.statement_id: Kata ini sudah ada dalam Inggris Kuno (Old English) puca; serupa Norse Kuno (Old Norse) púki, Kelt (Celtic): Wales (Welsh) pwca, Cornwall (Cornish) bucca, Irlandia (Irish) púca; Oxford English Dictionary condong Skandinavia, Erin Sebo dari Flinders University ke Irlandia. (Scandinavian)
claims.quote: The present-day English word is attested already in Old English as puca (with a diminutive form pucel ). Similar words are attested later in Old Norse (púki , with related forms including Old Swedish puke , Icelandic púki , and Frisian puk ) but also in the Celtic languages (Welsh pwca , Cornish bucca and Irish púca ).

claims.statement: Puck is also called the Goodfellows or Hobgoblin, Hob for Rob or Robin, from Robin Goodfellow.
claims.statement_id: Puck juga disebut Goodfellows atau Hobgoblin, Hob pengganti Rob atau Robin, dari Robin Goodfellow; seperti the good folk, untuk menyenangkan peri.
claims.quote: Puck may also be called The Goodfellows or Hobgoblin, in which Hob may substitute for Rob or Robin. This goes back to the character "Robin Goodfellow" and his name.

claims.statement: The earliest Robin Goodfellow reference in the Oxford English Dictionary is from 1531.
claims.statement_id: Rujukan tertua Robin Goodfellow menurut Oxford English Dictionary dari 1531.
claims.quote: The earliest reference to "Robin Goodfellow" cited by the Oxford English Dictionary is from 1531.

claims.statement: The Puk is a dwarfish (zwergenwüchsige) figure of Nordic legend (nordischen Volkssagen), living with people, among the elves (Elfen) of Germanic myth. Linked with the Celtic púca (keltischen Púca).
claims.statement_id: Puk sosok kerdil (zwergenwüchsige) dari legenda Nordik (nordischen Volkssagen), tinggal bersama manusia, golongan elf (Elfen) mitologi Jermanik (germanischen). Dikaitkan dengan púca Kelt (keltischen Púca).
claims.quote: ist eine zwergenwüchsige Figur unbestimmten Geschlechts der nordischen Volkssagen. Puks leben mit den Menschen zusammen und gehören in die Gruppe der Elfen aus der germanischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: A Puk given regular food and drink can bring prosperity; it is also linked with the Celtic púca.
claims.statement_id: Puk yang diberi makan-minum teratur dapat membawa kemakmuran; dikaitkan juga dengan púca Kelt.
claims.quote: Wird der Puk mit regelmäßigen Speisen und Getränken gut behandelt, so ist er, im Verbund mit anderen Sagengestalten wie Zwergen und Riesen, in der Lage, das Wohlergehen der Bewohner und deren Tiere positiv bis hin zum Reichtum zu beeinflussen.

claims.statement: Mistreated, the Puk causes grave harm, even madness or death.
claims.statement_id: Bila diperlakukan buruk, Puk mendatangkan kerugian besar, bahkan kegilaan atau kematian.
claims.quote: Wird er jedoch schlecht behandelt, fügt er den Bewohnern schwere Schäden zu, die nicht selten in Wahnsinn oder mit dem Tod enden.

claims.statement: The baobh-shìth (Scottish Gaelic) fairy witch, plural baobhan-sìth, is a female fairy of the Scottish Highlands, like the succubus; seduces then kills. (Highland)
claims.statement_id: Baobh-shìth (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic) penyihir peri, jamak baobhan-sìth, peri perempuan Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highlands), mirip succubus; merayu lalu membunuh korban; di Britania Raya. (Highland)
claims.quote: literally "fairy witch" or "fairy hag" in Scottish Gaelic, plural baobhan-sìth Scottish Gaelic pronunciation: [ˈpɤːvan ˈʃiː] ) is a female fairy in the folklore of the Scottish Highlands, though they also share certain characteristics in common with the succubus. They appear as beautiful women who seduce their victims before attacking them and killing them.

claims.statement: Many tales tell of hunters attacked in the wilds at night.
claims.statement_id: Banyak kisah: pemburu diserang di alam liar pada malam hari.
claims.quote: There are numerous stories about the baobhan-sìth with a general theme of hunters being attacked in the wilderness at night.

claims.statement: Katharine Briggs: the fourth man escaped thanks to iron horseshoes, a fairy weakness.
claims.statement_id: Katharine Briggs: lelaki keempat selamat karena besi tapal kuda, kelemahan peri.
claims.quote: Katharine Briggs suggested that the baobhan-sìth was unable to catch the fourth man among the horses because of the iron with which the horses were shod, iron being a traditional fairy vulnerability.

claims.statement: The women had deer hooves; his companions were found with throats cut.
claims.statement_id: Para perempuan berkaki kuku rusa; kawan-kawannya ditemukan tergorok.
claims.quote: In a similar tale one of the men noticed that the women had deer hooves instead of feet and fled from them. He returned the next morning to find that the other hunters had their "throats cut and chests laid open".

claims.statement: Macphee was protected by his dog, which drove the women off.
claims.statement_id: Macphee dilindungi anjingnya yang mengusir para perempuan.
claims.quote: Macphee was protected by his dog who drove the women from the cave.

claims.statement: Baobhan-Sith is the Scottish (schottische) term for a seductive female vampire (Vampirin) who kills young men; she appears in forests (Wald).
claims.statement_id: Baobhan-Sith istilah Skotlandia (schottische) untuk vampir perempuan penggoda (Vampirin) yang membunuh pemuda; muncul di hutan (Wald).
claims.quote: ist der schottische Begriff für eine verführerische Vampirin, die hübschen Jünglingen den Tod bringt. Sie tritt vor allem im Wald oder in der freien Natur auf.

claims.statement: In the tale recorded by Mackenzie, four hunters sheltered in a hut.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Mackenzie, empat pemburu bermalam di pondok.
claims.quote: In the tale recorded by Mackenzie, there were four men who went hunting and took shelter for the night in a lonely shieling or hut.

claims.statement: As a beautiful girl, often in green, she drains her victims to the last drop of blood.
claims.statement_id: Berwujud gadis cantik, sering berpakaian hijau, ia mengisap darah korban sampai tetes terakhir.
claims.quote: In der Gestalt eines wunderschönen, hauptsächlich, aber nicht zwingend grün gekleideten Mädchens erweckt sie keinerlei Argwohn, aber ihre Opfer saugt sie letztlich bis zum letzten Blutstropfen aus.

claims.statement: The boggart is a supernatural being of English folklore; Elizabeth Wright: a generic name for an apparition; Simon Young: any ambivalent or evil solitary spirit.
claims.statement_id: Boggart makhluk gaib cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore); Elizabeth Wright: nama umum penampakan; Simon Young: roh penyendiri ambivalen atau jahat; di Inggris Raya.
claims.quote: A boggart is a supernatural being from English folklore. The dialectologist Elizabeth Wright described the boggart as "a generic name for an apparition"; folklorist Simon Young defines it as "any ambivalent or evil solitary supernatural spirit."

claims.statement: Boggarts live indoors and outdoors, as household spirits or a genius loci; Lancashire Folklore (1867) by Harland and Wilkinson distinguishes house boggarts.
claims.statement_id: Boggart di dalam dan luar rumah, roh rumah atau genius loci; Lancashire Folklore (1867) Harland dan Wilkinson membedakan house boggarts.
claims.quote: Boggarts are found indoors and outdoors, as a household spirit, or a malevolent spirit defined by local geography, a genius loci inhabiting topographical features. The 1867 book Lancashire Folklore by Harland and Wilkinson makes a distinction between "house boggarts" and other types.

claims.statement: Boggarts are malevolent, creeping into beds, laying a clammy hand on faces, stripping sheets, following families who flee.
claims.statement_id: Boggart jahat, merangkak ke ranjang, menaruh tangan lembap di wajah, menarik seprai, mengikuti keluarga yang pindah.
claims.quote: Typical descriptions show boggarts to be malevolent. It is said that the boggart crawls into people's beds at night and puts a clammy hand on their faces. Sometimes he strips the bedsheets off them. The household boggart may follow a family wherever they flee.

claims.statement: A Lancashire source: a boggart must never be named or it becomes uncontrollable; in Yorkshire, boggard.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Lancashire: boggart tak boleh dinamai, atau ia jadi tak terkendali; di Yorkshire disebut boggard.
claims.quote: One Lancashire source reports the belief that a boggart should never be named: if the boggart was given a name, it could neither be reasoned with nor persuaded, but would become uncontrollable and destructive

claims.statement: From Middle English bugge; kin to bogle (Scots), bugbear, bogeyman.
claims.statement_id: Dari Inggris Pertengahan (Middle English) bugge; sekerabat dengan bogle (Scots), bugbear, bogeyman.
claims.quote: These forms all point to an origin with the Middle English word bugge (a spirit or monster) with an aggrandizing suffix making boggart, a great big bugge. This also makes boggart a close linguistic cousin of "bogle" (or boggle, a Scots variant), 'bugaboo', "bugbear", "bug", "bogeyman" and "bogie", all of which also derive from bugge.

claims.statement: Boggarts (bwcas, bogan, bogle) are creatures of British (britannique) folklore, ugly, hairy, spiteful dwarfs.
claims.statement_id: Boggart (bwcas, bogan, bogle) makhluk folklore Britania (britannique), kerdil buruk rupa, berbulu, jahat.
claims.quote: Les boggarts (ou bwcas, bogan, bogle, boggle) sont des créatures du folklore britannique. Ils y sont décrits comme des nains hideux, velus et malveillants.

claims.statement: Per Édouard Brasey, the boggart is the brownie's degenerate cousin.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Édouard Brasey, boggart sepupu brownie yang merosot.
claims.quote: Édouard Brasey prétend que le boggart serait dans l'imaginaire anglais le cousin dégénéré du brownie, un esprit servant britannique.

claims.statement: A horseshoe was hung before doors to keep boggarts away.
claims.statement_id: Tapal kuda digantung di depan pintu untuk mengusir boggart.
claims.quote: On suspendait parfois un fer à cheval devant les portes des maisons pour éloigner les boggarts.

claims.statement: The clurichaun (clúrachán, Irish clobhair-ceann) is a mischievous fairy of Irish folklore who loves drink and haunts cellars; related to the leprechaun.
claims.statement_id: Clurichaun (clúrachán, Irlandia/Irish clobhair-ceann) peri jahil cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore), gemar minum, menghantui gudang anggur; kerabat leprechaun; di Irlandia.
claims.quote: is a mischievous fairy in Irish folklore known for his great love of drinking and a tendency to haunt breweries, pubs and wine cellars. He is related to the leprechaun and has sometimes been conflated with him as a shoemaker and a guardian of hidden treasure. This has led some folklorists to suppose that the clurichaun is merely a leprechaun on a drinking spree

claims.statement: Like the leprechaun, the clurichaun is a solitary fairy.
claims.statement_id: Seperti leprechaun, clurichaun peri penyendiri.
claims.quote: Like the leprechaun, the clurichaun is a solitary fairy, encountered alone rather than in groups, as distinct from the trooping fairies.

claims.statement: In The Haunted Cellar (Thomas Crofton Croker, 1825), Naggeneen haunts an Irish lord's cellar, 6 in tall, face like a withered apple.
claims.statement_id: Dalam The Haunted Cellar (Croker, Thomas Crofton Croker, 1825), Naggeneen menghantui gudang anggur bangsawan Irlandia (Irish), setinggi 15 cm, wajah seperti apel layu; topi merah, gesper perak.
claims.quote: In the folktale "The Haunted Cellar", recorded by Thomas Crofton Croker in 1825, a clurichaun named Naggeneen haunts the wine cellar of an Irish lord, drinking everything in sight and playing frightening pranks on the servants. He is described as a little man measuring 6 in (150 mm) tall, with a face like a withered apple.

claims.statement: Clurichauns pass through keyholes, turn rushes into horses and fly on rushes.
claims.statement_id: Clurichaun melewati lubang kunci, mengubah rumput rawa jadi kuda, terbang dengan rumput.
claims.quote: In this story, the clurichaun is able to pass through keyholes to invade homes and wine cellars and can transform bog rushes into horses to be used as mounts. Clurichauns can also fly through the air on rushes similar to witches and their broomsticks.

claims.statement: In Master and Man, Billy Mac Daniel must serve seven years and a day, freed by invoking God's blessing.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Master and Man, Billy Mac Daniel dipaksa melayani tujuh tahun satu hari, terbebas dengan berkat Tuhan (God).
claims.quote: He takes the drink but when he refuses to pay for it he is compelled by the clurichaun to serve him for seven years and a day. Billy, however, is eventually able to break his servitude by invoking the blessing of God.

claims.statement: The Cluricaun is an elf being (Elfenwesen) of Irish (Irlands) Celtic myth, fond of drink, haunting wine cellars (Weinkellern), much like the Leprechaun.
claims.statement_id: Cluricaun makhluk elf (Elfenwesen) mitologi Kelt Irlandia (Irlands), gemar minum, menghantui gudang anggur (Weinkellern), mirip Leprechaun.
claims.quote: ist ein Elfenwesen aus der keltischen Mythologie Irlands. Er ist bekannt für seine Vorliebe, viel zu trinken und in Brauereien, Kneipen und Weinkellern zu spuken. Er ist dem Leprechaun sehr ähnlich

claims.statement: Thomas Crofton Croker (1825) derived the word from luchramán, dwarf (Zwerg); the Brothers Grimm (Brüder Grimm) translated his tales in 1826 as Irische Elfenmärchen.
claims.statement_id: Thomas Crofton Croker (1825) menurunkan kata dari luchramán, kerdil (Zwerg); diterjemahkan Grimm bersaudara (Brüder Grimm) 1826 sebagai Irische Elfenmärchen.
claims.quote: Thomas Crofton Croker behauptete 1825 in Fairy Legends and Traditions of the South of Ireland, das Wort sei von „luchramán“, Zwerg, abgeleitet. Seine Märchensammlung wurde durch die Brüder Grimm 1826 als Irische Elfenmärchen übersetzt

claims.statement: Manawydan fab Llŷr is a Welsh figure, son of Llŷr, brother of Brân the Blessed and Brânwen; his name is cognate with the Irish sea god Manannán mac Lir.
claims.statement_id: Manawydan fab Llŷr tokoh mitologi Wales (Welsh), putra Llŷr, saudara Brân the Blessed dan Brânwen; namanya sekerabat dengan dewa laut Irlandia (Irish) Manannán mac Lir, dari dewa Kelt (Celtic) yang sama; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Manawydan fab Llŷr is a figure of Welsh mythology, the son of Llŷr and the brother of Brân the Blessed and Brânwen. The first element in his name is cognate with the stem of the name of the Irish sea god Manannán mac Lir, and likely originated from the same Celtic deity as Manannán.

claims.statement: His main appearances are in the Second and Third Branches of the Mabinogi; also the Welsh Triads.
claims.statement_id: Penampilan terpenting di Cabang Kedua dan Ketiga (Second and Third Branches) Mabinogi; juga Welsh Triads.
claims.quote: Manawydan's most important appearances occur in the Second and Third Branches of the Mabinogi (the latter of which is named for him), but he is also referenced frequently in medieval poetry and the Welsh Triads.

claims.statement: Manawydan advises Brân the Blessed, King of Britain.
claims.statement_id: Manawydan penasihat Brân the Blessed, raja Britania (King of Britain).
claims.quote: In this tale, Manawydan serves as advisor to his brother Brân the Blessed, the King of Britain.

claims.statement: Manawydan is one of seven survivors; they take Brân's head back to Britain. (Ireland)
claims.statement_id: Manawydan salah satu dari tujuh penyintas; membawa kepala Brân ke Britania (Britain); perang di Irlandia. (Ireland)
claims.quote: In the ensuing war, Manawydan is one of only seven men to survive. The mortally wounded Brân asks Manawydan and the others to cut off his head and take it back to Britain

claims.statement: In the Third Branch Pryderi invites him to Dyfed and to marry Rhiannon; a spell empties Dyfed.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Cabang Ketiga Pryderi mengajaknya tinggal di Dyfed dan menikahi Rhiannon; mantra melenyapkan orang dan ternak Dyfed.
claims.quote: one of Manawydan's fellow survivors, Pryderi, invites him to live with him in Dyfed and marry Rhiannon, Pryderi's mother

claims.statement: In the Mabinogion he is a peaceable scholar (Gelehrter) and magician (Zauberer); like Manannan mac Lir he is seen as a sea god (Meeresgott); per Birkhan the name comes from Manaw, Welsh for the Isle of Man.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mabinogion ia cendekiawan (Gelehrter) dan penyihir (Zauberer) cinta damai; seperti Manannan mac Lir ia juga dewa laut (Meeresgott); menurut Birkhan nama dari Manaw, nama Wales untuk Isle of Man.
claims.quote: ist eine Figur aus walisischen Sagen, wie dem Mabinogion, wo er als friedfertiger Gelehrter und Zauberer dargestellt wird. Wie sein irischer Namensvetter Manannan mac Lir von den Túatha Dé Danann wird er auch als Meeresgott gesehen, nach Birkhan leitet sich der Name Manawydan von Manaw, dem kymrischen Namen der Isle of Man, ab.

claims.statement: The afanc (Addanc) is a Welsh lake monster resembling a crocodile, beaver, dwarf or platypus, sometimes a demon.
claims.statement_id: Afanc (Addanc) monster danau mitologi Wales (Welsh), mirip buaya, berang-berang, kerdil, platipus, atau iblis; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is a lake monster from Welsh mythology. Its exact description varies, being described as resembling a crocodile, beaver or dwarf-like creature, or a platypus and is sometimes said to be a demon.

claims.statement: It lives in Llyn Llion, Llyn Barfog, near Brynberian Bridge or Llyn yr Afanc on the Afon Conwy near Betws-y-coed.
claims.statement_id: Tempatnya Llyn Llion, Llyn Barfog, dekat Brynberian Bridge, atau Llyn yr Afanc di Afon Conwy dekat Betws-y-coed.
claims.quote: The lake in which it dwells is also uncertain and it is variously said to live in Llyn Llion, Llyn Barfog, near Brynberian Bridge or in Llyn yr Afanc, a pool on the Afon Conwy near Betws-y-coed that was named after the creature.

claims.statement: The afanc preys on anyone falling or swimming in its lake.
claims.statement_id: Afanc memangsa siapa pun yang jatuh atau berenang di danaunya.
claims.quote: The afanc was a monstrous creature that, like most lake monsters, was said to prey upon any foolish enough to fall into or swim in its lake.

claims.statement: Synonyms are Afanc, Addane, Adanc, Avanc, Abhac, Abac.
claims.statement_id: Sinonimnya Afanc, Addane, Adanc, Avanc, Abhac, Abac.
claims.quote: Es existieren mehrere Synonyme für das Wesen, wie etwa Afanc [ ˈavaŋk] (wohl das gebräuchlichste), Addane, Adanc, Avanc, Abhac und Abac.

claims.statement: Its very tough hide (sehr starke Haut) is hard to wound with ordinary weapons.
claims.statement_id: Kulitnya sangat kuat (sehr starke Haut), sulit dilukai senjata biasa.
claims.quote: Es besitzt eine sehr starke Haut, was es sehr schwer, wenn nicht gar unmöglich macht, es mit herkömmlichen Waffen zu verletzen.

claims.statement: A maiden (Jungfrau) let it sleep in her lap and villagers chained it; on waking it crushed her.
claims.statement_id: Seorang gadis (Jungfrau) membiarkannya tidur di pangkuan, penduduk desa merantainya; saat bangun ia meremukkan gadis itu.
claims.quote: Von einer anderen Sage wird erzählt, in der eine Jungfrau es bezwang, indem sie es in ihrem Schoß schlafen ließ; sogleich eilten die Dorfbewohner herbei und legten das Untier in Ketten. Als es erwachte, geriet es in Zorn und zerschmetterte rasend das Mädchen, in dessen Schoß es noch immer lag.

claims.statement: It was dragged to Cwm Ffynnon or killed by Peredur; later legends credit King Arthur (König Artus) or Parzival. (British, britischen)
claims.statement_id: Akhirnya diseret ke danau Cwm Ffynnon atau dibunuh Peredur; legenda kemudian menyebut Raja Arthur (König Artus) atau Parzival. (British, britischen)
claims.quote: Am Ende wurde es entweder in den See Cwm Ffynnon gezogen oder aber von Peredur getötet. In späteren britischen Legenden wird die Tötung der Kreatur entweder König Artus oder Parzival (der Name Peredurs in der Artussage) zugesprochen.

claims.statement: Per Edward Williams the Addanc was dragged from Llyn Llion by Hu Gadarn's oxen and easily killed on land.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Edward Williams, Addanc ditarik keluar dari Llyn Llion oleh lembu Hu Gadarn dan mudah dibunuh di darat.
claims.quote: Einer anderen Fassung von Williams zufolge wurde das Addanc von den Ochsen des Hu Gadarn aus dem See in Llyn Llion gezogen, und konnte, sobald es nicht mehr im Wasser schwamm, leicht getötet werden.

claims.statement: Bedd yr Afanc (Grave of the Monster, Grab des Ungeheuers), the only gallery grave (Galeriegrab) in Wales, is linked to the Addanc.
claims.statement_id: Bedd yr Afanc (Makam Monster, Grab des Ungeheuers), satu-satunya makam galeri (Galeriegrab) di Wales, dikaitkan dengan Addanc.
claims.quote: Bedd yr Afanc („Das Grab des Ungeheuers“) ist das einzige in Wales zu findende Galeriegrab und wird mit Addanc verbunden.

claims.statement: Black Annis (Black Agnes, Black Anna) is a bogeywoman of English folklore, a blue-faced iron-clawed hag eating children, in a Dane Hills cave in Leicestershire.
claims.statement_id: Black Annis (Black Agnes, Black Anna) momok perempuan cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), nenek sihir berwajah biru bercakar besi pemakan anak, di gua Dane Hills, Leicestershire; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Black Annis (also known as Black Agnes or Black Anna) is a bogeywoman figure in English folklore. She is imagined as a blue-faced hag or witch with iron claws and a taste for human flesh (especially children). She is said to haunt the countryside of Leicestershire, living in a cave in the Dane Hills with a great oak tree at the entrance.

claims.statement: She goes out at night for children and lambs, tans their skins, wears them at her waist.
claims.statement_id: Keluar malam mencari anak dan anak domba, menyamak kulitnya, memakainya di pinggang.
claims.quote: She is said to venture out at night looking for unsuspecting children and lambs to eat, then tanning their skins by hanging them on a tree before wearing them around her waist.

claims.statement: Leicestershire cottages had small windows; her howl was heard 8 km away.
claims.statement_id: Pondok Leicestershire berjendela kecil; lolongannya terdengar 8 km.
claims.quote: It is said that cottages in Leicestershire were purposely built with small windows so that Black Annis could only get a single arm inside. When she howled, she could be heard 5 mi (8.0 km) away

claims.statement: Earliest reference: an 18th-century deed, Black Anny's Bower Close; County Folklore (1895) cites two 1764 deeds.
claims.statement_id: Rujukan tertua: akta tanah abad ke-18, Black Anny's Bower Close; County Folklore (1895) menyebut dua akta 1764.
claims.quote: The earliest known written reference to Black Annis was from an eighteenth century title deed that referred to a parcel of land (or "close") as "Black Anny's Bower Close". The first volume of County Folklore (1895), published by The Folklore Society, mentions two such title deeds dated May 13th and 14th, 1764.

claims.statement: T. C. Lethbridge: origin in Celtic mythology, Danu (Anu).
claims.statement_id: T. C. Lethbridge: asal dari mitologi Kelt (Celtic), Danu (Anu).
claims.quote: Some have claimed, as T. C. Lethbridge did, that the origin can be found in Celtic mythology based on Danu (or Anu) or it may derive from Germanic mythology (see Hel).

claims.statement: Ronald Hutton disagrees with such theories.
claims.statement_id: Ronald Hutton tidak sependapat dengan teori itu.
claims.quote: Ronald Hutton however disagrees with such theories in his book The Triumph of the Moon

claims.statement: She was also seen as a cat (Katze).
claims.statement_id: Ia juga pernah terlihat sebagai kucing (Katze).
claims.quote: Auch als Katze soll sie gesehen worden sein.

claims.statement: Parents (Eltern) use Black Annis to frighten disobedient children.
claims.statement_id: Orang tua (Eltern) memakai Black Annis untuk menakuti anak yang tidak patuh.
claims.quote: Die Figur der Black Annis wird deshalb von Eltern als Drohgespenst verwendet, um unfolgsame Kinder zum Gehorsam zu bringen.

claims.statement: The blue men of the Minch (storm kelpies, Scottish Gaelic na fir ghorma) inhabit the waters between the northern Outer Hebrides and mainland Scotland, drowning sailors. (Kelpie)
claims.statement_id: Blue men of the Minch (storm kelpies, Gaelik Skotlandia/Scottish Gaelic na fir ghorma) makhluk mitologi perairan antara Outer Hebrides utara dan daratan Skotlandia (Scotland), menenggelamkan pelaut; di Britania Raya. (Kelpie)
claims.quote: The blue men of the Minch, also known as storm kelpies (Scottish Gaelic: na fir ghorma Scottish Gaelic pronunciation: [nə fiɾʲ ˈɣɔɾɔmə] ), are mythological creatures inhabiting the stretch of water between the northern Outer Hebrides and mainland Scotland, looking for sailors to drown and stricken boats to sink.

claims.statement: Blue but humanlike, human-sized; they create storms and float asleep in fair weather.
claims.statement_id: Biru tapi mirip manusia, seukuran manusia; menciptakan badai; tidur mengapung saat cerah; berenang seperti lumba-lumba.
claims.quote: Apart from their blue colour, the mythical creatures look much like humans, and are about the same size. They have the power to create storms, but when the weather is fine they float sleeping on or just below the surface of the water.

claims.statement: Their chief shouts two lines of verse; if the skipper fails to complete it, they capsize the ship.
claims.statement_id: Pemimpinnya meneriakkan dua baris puisi; jika nakhoda gagal melengkapinya, kapal dibalikkan.
claims.quote: They are able to speak, and when a group approaches a ship its chief may shout two lines of poetry to the master of the vessel and challenge him to complete the verse. If the skipper fails in that task then the blue men will attempt to capsize his ship.

claims.statement: Explanations: a personification of the sea, or the painted Picts; also North African slaves brought by the Vikings.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan: personifikasi laut, atau bangsa Pict (Picts) bertubuh dicat; juga budak Afrika Utara (North African) yang dibawa Viking (Vikings) ke Skotlandia.
claims.quote: Suggestions to explain the mythical blue men include that they may be a personification of the sea, or originate with the Picts, whose painted bodies may have given the impression of men raising themselves out of the water

claims.statement: Per Donald A. Mackenzie they have no counterparts elsewhere, even in Scotland.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Donald A. Mackenzie tak ada padanannya di tempat lain di Skotlandia (Scotland).
claims.quote: According to Donald A. Mackenzie they have no counterparts elsewhere in the world or even in other areas of Scotland

claims.statement: Perhaps from a tribe of fallen angels (ángeles caídos) split in three: land fairies, sea blue men, the merry dancers (bailarines felices) of the Aurora.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin bagian suku malaikat jatuh (ángeles caídos) yang terpecah tiga: peri darat, orang biru laut, penari riang (bailarines felices) Aurora di langit.
claims.quote: Los hombres azules podrían haber sido parte de una tribu de "ángeles caídos" que se dividieron en tres; la primera se convirtió en las hadas de la tierra, la segunda se convirtió en los hombres azules del mar, y los restantes se convirtieron en los "bailarines felices" de la Aurora polar en el cielo.

claims.statement: The blue men (hombres azules) may personify the sea (mar) or come from the Picts (pictos).
claims.statement_id: Orang biru (hombres azules) mungkin personifikasi laut (mar) atau berasal dari Pict (pictos).
claims.quote: Se ha sugerido que los hombres azules míticos puedan ser una personificación del mar, o que tienen su origen en los pictos

claims.statement: In Celtic mythology Dea Matrona, Divine Mother, gave her name to the river Marne (Matrŏna) in Gaul. (France)
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Kelt (Celtic), Dea Matrona, Ibu Ilahi, memberi nama Sungai Marne (Matrŏna) di Galia (Gaul); di Prancis. (France)
claims.quote: In Celtic mythology, Dea Matrona ('Divine Mother') was the goddess who gives her name to the river Marne (ancient Matrŏna) in Gaul.

claims.statement: The Gaulish name Mātr-on-ā means Great Mother; she is read as a mother goddess.
claims.statement_id: Nama Galia (Gaulish) Mātr-on-ā berarti Ibu Agung; ditafsirkan sebagai dewi ibu.
claims.quote: The Gaulish theonym Mātr-on-ā signifies 'Great Mother' and the goddess of the Marne has been interpreted to be a mother goddess.

claims.statement: Gaulish images show mother goddesses nursing or holding fruit or dogs; Matronae appear in threes or twos.
claims.statement_id: Gambar Galia menunjukkan dewi ibu menyusui atau memangku buah atau anjing; Matronae (Matres and Matronae) bertiga atau berdua.
claims.quote: Many Gaulish religious images—including inexpensive terracotta statues mass-produced for use in household shrines—depict mother goddesses nursing babies or holding fruits, other foods, or small dogs in their laps. In many areas, such Matronae were depicted in groups of three (or sometimes two)

claims.statement: The Welsh Modron, mother of Mabon, comes from the same etymon.
claims.statement_id: Nama Modron (Wales/Welsh), ibu Mabon, dari akar yang sama.
claims.quote: The name of Welsh mythological figure Modron, mother of Mabon, is derived from the same etymon (and Mabon has a cognate in Gaulish Maponos).

claims.statement: Matrona is a river goddess (Flussgöttin), personifying the Marne (Flusses Marne); an 1831 inscription at La Marnotte near Bellesmes, Haute-Marne, Langres.
claims.statement_id: Matrona dewi sungai (Flussgöttin), personifikasi Sungai Marne (Flusses Marne); prasasti 1831 di La Marnotte dekat Bellesmes, Haute-Marne, Langres.
claims.quote: Matrona oder Dea Matrona ist der Name einer Flussgöttin, die als Personifizierung des Flusses Marne verstanden wird. Ihre Verehrung wird durch eine Weiheinschrift bezeugt, die 1831 im Quellgebiet des Flusses („La Marnotte“) bei Bellesmes (Département Haute-Marne) in der Nähe von Langres

claims.statement: Gaius Iulius Caesar in De bello Gallico named Matrona as the Marne, bordering Gaul (Gallien) and Belgica with the Sequana (Seine).
claims.statement_id: Gaius Iulius Caesar dalam De bello Gallico menyebut Matrona nama Sungai Marne, bersama Sequana (Seine) batas Galia (Gallien) dan Belgica.
claims.quote: Der römische Feldherr Gaius Iulius Caesar erwähnte in seinem Bericht De bello Gallico (1. Buch, 1) über den Gallischen Krieg (58 bis 51/50 v. Chr.) Matrona als Namen des Flusses Marne, der zusammen mit dem Unterlauf der Sequana (Seine) die Grenze zwischen dem Kernland Gallien und der römischen Provinz Belgica im Norden bildete.

claims.statement: Matrona is of Celtic (keltischen) origin, from Gaulish (gallischen) mātīr, mother (Mutter).
claims.statement_id: Nama Matrona asal Kelt (keltischen), dari Galia (gallischen) mātīr, ibu (Mutter).
claims.quote: Der Name Matrona ist keltischen Ursprungs, abgeleitet vom gallischen mātīr (Mutter)

claims.statement: The Dobhar-chú (King otter) is a creature of Irish and Scottish folklore like a dog and an otter, with protective fur, living in water.
claims.statement_id: Dobhar-chú (King otter) makhluk cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish) dan Skotlandia (Scottish), mirip anjing dan berang-berang, berbulu pelindung, hidup di air; di Irlandia.
claims.quote: or King otter, is a creature of Irish and Scottish folklore. It resembles both a dog and an otter, though it sometimes is described as half dog, half fish. It is said to possess fur with protective properties and live in the water.

claims.statement: Its legend relies on oral tradition.
claims.statement_id: Legendanya bergantung pada tradisi lisan.
claims.quote: Its legend has relied heavily on oral storytelling and tradition, and there have been little to no written records of the Dobhar-chú.

claims.statement: Dobharchú is one of the two most common Irish words for otter; also dobarcu, doyarchu.
claims.statement_id: Dobharchú salah satu kata Irlandia (Irish) untuk berang-berang; juga dobarcu, doyarchu.
claims.quote: Dobharchú is one of the two most common Irish words for "otter".

claims.statement: Like an otter five times larger (3–4.6 m), white pelt, black ear tips, a black cross on its back.
claims.statement_id: Mirip berang-berang, lima kali lebih besar (3–4,6 m), berbulu putih, ujung telinga hitam, tanda salib hitam.
claims.quote: The Dobhar-chú is described as resembling an otter, though about five times as large at 10–15 ft (3.0–4.6 m), with a white pelt, black ear tips, and a shape like a black cross on its back.

claims.statement: A headstone in Congbháil (Conwall) Cemetery, Glenade, County Leitrim, depicts the Dobhar-chú.
claims.statement_id: Batu nisan di Congbháil (Conwall) Cemetery, Glenade, County Leitrim, menggambarkan Dobhar-chú.
claims.quote: A headstone, found in Congbháil (Conwall) Cemetery in Glenade, County Leitrim, depicts the Dobhar-chú. It is related to a story of an attack on a local woman by the creature.

claims.statement: In 1722 Grace McGloighlin at Glenade Lough; Terrence found her mutilated and killed the Dobhar-chú with a dagger; its mate rose.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1722 Grace McGloighlin di Glenade Lough; Terrence menemukannya tercabik, membunuh Dobhar-chú dengan belati; pasangannya muncul.
claims.quote: Both accounts assert that upon Mr. McGloighlin's arrival, he discovered her mutilated body with the Dobhar-chú sleeping on top. Terrence ran home and, bringing a dagger with him, killed the Dobhar-chú. As the beast died, it let out a whistling yell to its mate, who soon rose from the lough.

claims.statement: Per the es article the stone belongs to a woman named Gráinne killed in the 17th century (siglo XVII).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel es, nisan itu milik perempuan bernama Gráinne yang dibunuh pada abad ke-17 (siglo XVII).
claims.quote: La lápida se afirma es de la mujer asesinada por el Dobhar-chú en el siglo XVII. Su nombre se dice era Gráinne.

claims.statement: The husband stabbed the Dobhar-chú in the heart; dying, it whistled and another came out.
claims.statement_id: Suaminya menikam jantung Dobhar-chú; saat sekarat ia bersiul memanggil yang lain.
claims.quote: El hombre mató al Dobhar-chú, acuchillando en el corazón. Mientras moría,  emitía un silbido que hizo que otro saliera del agua.

claims.statement: The Fairy Queen (Queen of the Fairies) is a female ruler of fairies, sometimes with a king; named Titania or Mab.
claims.statement_id: Fairy Queen (Queen of the Fairies) penguasa perempuan peri, kadang berpasangan raja; nama Titania dan Mab; di Britania dan Irlandia.
claims.quote: In folklore and literature, the Fairy Queen or Queen of the Fairies is a female ruler of the fairies, sometimes but not always paired with a king. Depending on the work, she may be named or unnamed; Titania and Mab are two frequently used names.

claims.statement: The Tuatha Dé Danann and Daoine Sidhe of Irish myth had many kings and queens; Oonagh (Una, Nuala) was wife of Finvarra, fairy king of western Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Tuatha Dé Danann dan Daoine Sidhe mitologi Irlandia (Irish) punya banyak raja-ratu; Oonagh (Una, Nuala) istri Finvarra, raja peri Irlandia (Ireland) barat.
claims.quote: The Tuatha Dé Danann and the Daoine Sidhe of Irish mythology had numerous local kings and queens. Oonagh, Una or Nuala was the wife of Finvarra or Fionnbharr, the fairy king of western Ireland

claims.statement: Other Irish fairy queens: Clíodhna of Munster, Aibhell, Ainé.
claims.statement_id: Ratu peri Irlandia lain: Clíodhna dari Munster, Aibhell, Ainé.
claims.quote: Other Irish fairy queens included Clíodhna of Munster, Aibhell and Ainé.

claims.statement: Arthurian Morgan le Fey ruled Avalon and was sometimes a fairy queen; in the Vita Merlini, Morgen heads nine queens.
claims.statement_id: Morgan le Fey (Arthurian) memerintah Avalon, kadang ratu peri; dalam Vita Merlini, Morgen kepala sembilan ratu.
claims.quote: The Arthurian character of Morgan le Fey (or Morgan of the Fairies) ruled the supernatural island of Avalon and was sometimes depicted as a fairy queen. In the Vita Merlini , she is Morgen, the chief of nine magical sister queens.

claims.statement: A kind fairy queen in Alison Gross, a deadly one in Tam Lin who pays a tithe to Hell every seven years; Child Ballads.
claims.statement_id: Ratu peri baik dalam Alison Gross, kejam dalam Tam Lin yang membayar upeti ke Neraka (Hell) tiap tujuh tahun; Child Ballads.
claims.quote: A kind and helpful fairy queen features in Alison Gross (Child 35), and a terrible and deadly fairy queen is the antagonist of Tam Lin (Child 39). Tam Lin's Fairy Queen pays a tithe to Hell every seven years

claims.statement: In Thomas the Rhymer a fairy queen takes Thomas as lover and gives him prophetic powers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Thomas the Rhymer ratu peri menjadikan Thomas kekasih dan memberinya kemampuan bernubuat.
claims.quote: An unnamed fairy queen appears in Thomas the Rhymer (Child 37), where she takes the titular character as her lover and leaves him with prophetic abilities.

claims.statement: Fairy queens (reinas de las hadas) appear in the Child Ballads, 305 folk ballads of England (Inglaterra) and Scotland (Escocia) collected by Francis James Child.
claims.statement_id: Reina de las hadas muncul dalam Child Ballads, 305 balada rakyat Inggris (Inglaterra) dan Skotlandia (Escocia) himpunan Francis James Child.
claims.quote: Las reinas de las hadas aparecen en algunas de las Baladas Infantiles, un conjunto de 305 baladas populares de Inglaterra y Escocia recopiladas por Francis James Child.

claims.statement: Fand (tear) or Fann (weak person) is an otherworldly woman of Irish mythology.
claims.statement_id: Fand (air mata) atau Fann (orang lemah), perempuan dunia lain mitologi Irlandia (Irish); di Irlandia.
claims.quote: Fand ("tear", "teardrop of beauty") or Fann ("weak, helpless person'") is an otherworldly woman in Irish mythology. The two forms of her name are not phonetic variants, but two different words of different meaning and the history of her name is debated.

claims.statement: In Serglige Con Culainn (Ulster Cycle), daughter of Áed Abrat, sister of Lí Ban, wife of Manannán (Manannán mac Lir).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Serglige Con Culainn (Siklus Ulster, Ulster Cycle), putri Áed Abrat, saudari Lí Ban, istri Manannán (Manannán mac Lir).
claims.quote: Fand appears most prominently in the Ulster Cycle tale, Serglige Con Culainn ("The Sickbed of Cúchulainn") as the daughter of Áed Abrat, sister of Lí Ban and one Angus, and wife of Manannán.

claims.statement: Fand appears as an otherworldly seabird, flying with Lí Ban joined by a gold chain.
claims.statement_id: Fand berwujud burung laut dunia lain, terbang bersama Lí Ban dengan rantai emas.
claims.quote: She enters the story in the form of an otherworldly sea bird. In her sea bird form, she flies with a flock of enchanted birds, with each pair joined together by a silver chain. Fand, flying with her sister Lí Ban, stands out from the rest as they are connected by a gold chain.

claims.statement: They whip Cúchulainn until he lies sick a year; later Cúchulainn and Fand become lovers.
claims.statement_id: Mereka mencambuk Cúchulainn hingga ia sakit setahun; kemudian Cúchulainn dan Fand menjadi kekasih.
claims.quote: Later, Fand and Lí Ban return in the form of "Otherworldly women" and confront him on the shore of the lake. They beat Cúchulainn with horsewhips until he falls ill and lies abed for a year, unable to rise.

claims.statement: Emer is jealous; Fand returns to Manannán, who shakes his cloak of mists between Fand and Cúchulainn.
claims.statement_id: Emer cemburu; Fand kembali kepada Manannán yang mengibaskan jubah kabut di antara Fand dan Cúchulainn.
claims.quote: She chants a poem, and then returns to her husband Manannán, who shakes his magical cloak of mists between Fand and Cúchulainn, that they may never meet again.

claims.statement: Fand is daughter of Aed Abrath of the Túatha Dé Danann, a sea goddess (Meeresgöttin), queen of the elves (Königin der Elfen), loveliest of goddesses.
claims.statement_id: Fand putri Aed Abrath dari Túatha Dé Danann, dewi laut (Meeresgöttin), ratu elf (Königin der Elfen), dewi tercantik.
claims.quote: Sie gilt als Tochter Aed Abraths von den Túatha Dé Danann, ist eine Meeresgöttin, aber auch Königin der Elfen und soll die schönste aller Göttinnen sein.

claims.statement: Cúchulainn and Fand become lovers; his wife Emer, jealous, attacks with knife-armed women.
claims.statement_id: Cúchulainn dan Fand menjadi kekasih; Emer, istri Cúchulainn, cemburu dan menyerang dengan perempuan bersenjata pisau.
claims.quote: Cúchulainn and Fand then become lovers. The relationship does not last, as Cúchulainn's wife, Emer is very jealous and comes to attack the couple with a troop of women armed with knives.

claims.statement: Grannus (Grannos) was a Celtic healing god of Gaul, the Germanies, Raetia and the Danube, with dedications from Britain, Hispania, Rome; identified with Apollo (Apollo Grannus).
claims.statement_id: Grannus (Grannos) dewa penyembuhan Kelt (Celtic), dipuja di Galia (Gaul), Germania (Germanies), Raetia, Danube, juga Britania (Britain), Hispania, Roma (Rome), Rhine; Romawi (Roman) menyamakannya dengan Apollo (Apollo Grannus); di Prancis dan Jerman.
claims.quote: was an ancient Celtic healing god associated with springs and curative waters. He was worshipped in Gaul, the two Germanies, Raetia and the Danube provinces, with scattered dedications from Britain, Hispania, Rome and beyond the Rhine frontier. In the Roman period he was most often identified with Apollo through the interpretatio romana and appears in inscriptions as Apollo Grannus.

claims.statement: Named in about thirty Latin dedications, a Greek inscription from Ephesus, and by Cassius Dio.
claims.statement_id: Disebut dalam sekitar tiga puluh prasasti Latin (Latin), prasasti Yunani (Greek) di Ephesus, dan oleh Cassius Dio.
claims.quote: He is named in about thirty Latin dedications, in a Greek honorific inscription from Ephesus, and by the historian Cassius Dio, who records that the emperor Caracalla sought his aid.

claims.statement: The name is linked to Proto-Celtic for beard, the bearded one.
claims.statement_id: Nama dikaitkan dengan Proto-Kelt (Proto-Celtic) untuk janggut, yang berjanggut.
claims.quote: One line of interpretation connects the name with Proto-Celtic *grand- (or *grend- ), meaning 'beard'. On this reading Grannus would mean roughly 'the bearded one'.

claims.statement: Aquae Granni, the waters of Grannus, lies behind the name of Aachen.
claims.statement_id: Aquae Granni, perairan Grannus, asal nama Aachen.
claims.quote: Place-names include Aquae Granni ('the waters of Grannus'), which lies behind the modern name of Aachen

claims.statement: Hot springs at Aquae Granni (Aachen) were likely his; Cassius Dio: Caracalla appealed to Apollo Grannus, Asclepius and Serapis without relief. (German)
claims.statement_id: Mata air panas Aquae Granni (Aachen) diduga untuk Grannus; Cassius Dio: Caracalla memohon kepada Apollo Grannus, Asclepius, Serapis tanpa hasil; di Jerman. (German)
claims.quote: Hot springs such as those at Aquae Granni (today's Aachen) are thought to have been dedicated to Grannus. The clearest statement of Grannus's character comes from Cassius Dio, who lists Apollo Grannus with Asclepius and Serapis among the healing gods to whom Caracalla appealed, without relief, during his illness.

claims.statement: Grannus (Grannos) was a Celtic healing god (Heilgottes der Kelten), equated with Apollon by the Interpretatio Romana; his partner was Sirona.
claims.statement_id: Grannus (Grannos) dewa penyembuh Kelt (Heilgottes der Kelten), disamakan dengan Apollon menurut Interpretatio Romana; pasangannya Sirona.
claims.quote: ist der Name eines Heilgottes der Kelten und wurde nach der Interpretatio Romana mit Apollon gleichgesetzt. Seine Partnerin war die Göttin Sirona.

claims.statement: Grannus was the most widespread Celtic god; centred in Lower (Niedergermanien) and Upper Germany (Obergermanien) and Raetia.
claims.statement_id: Grannus dewa Kelt (keltische Gott) dengan penyebaran terluas; pusat di Germania Bawah (Niedergermanien), Germania Atas (Obergermanien), Raetia.
claims.quote: Grannus war offenbar der keltische Gott mit der größten Ausbreitung. Das Zentrum seiner Verehrung lag in den Provinzen Niedergermanien, Obergermanien und Raetia, inklusive der Agri decumates.

claims.statement: At Faimingen stands the Apollo-Grannus temple (Apollo-Grannus-Tempel) endowed by Emperor (Kaiser) Caracalla.
claims.statement_id: Di Faimingen berdiri kuil Apollo-Grannus (Apollo-Grannus-Tempel) yang didirikan kaisar (Kaiser) Caracalla.
claims.quote: In Faimingen steht der von Kaiser Caracalla gestiftete Apollo-Grannus-Tempel.

claims.statement: The liver bird is a mythical creature symbolising the English city of Liverpool, shown as a cormorant bearing laver seaweed.
claims.statement_id: Liver bird makhluk mitos lambang kota Inggris (English) Liverpool, digambarkan kormoran membawa rumput laut laver; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is a mythical creature that is the symbol of the English city of Liverpool. It is normally represented as a cormorant, and appears as such on the city's arms, in which it bears a branch of laver seaweed in its beak as a further pun on the name "Liverpool".

claims.statement: The seal (1352) showed a bird with a scroll reading JOHIS, meant as an eagle of John the Evangelist.
claims.statement_id: Segel (1352) bergambar burung dengan gulungan JOHIS; dimaksudkan elang lambang Yohanes Penginjil (John the Evangelist).
claims.quote: The seal depicted a generic bird with a plant sprig in its beak, together with a scroll inscribed (in shaky letters) "JOHIS" - an abbreviation for Johannis, Latin for "John's". The bird was almost certainly intended to be an eagle, the symbol of John the Evangelist

claims.statement: By the 17th century its identity was forgotten, read as a cormorant or lever.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-17 identitasnya terlupa, ditafsirkan kormoran atau lever.
claims.quote: By the 17th century the bird's real identity had been forgotten: it began to be interpreted either as a cormorant, a common bird in the area, or as a "lever".

claims.statement: Modern popularity dates from 1911, when the Royal Liver Building was built with two liver birds.
claims.statement_id: Popularitas modern sejak 1911, saat Royal Liver Building (Liver Building) dibangun dengan dua liver bird.
claims.quote: The modern popularity of the symbol largely dates to 1911, when the Liver Building was built. This prominent display of two liver birds rekindled the idea that the liver was a mythical bird that once haunted the local shoreline.

claims.statement: Legend: a pair, the female watching the sea for sailors, the male guarding families in the city.
claims.statement_id: Legenda: sepasang, betina memandang laut menunggu pelaut, jantan menjaga keluarga di kota.
claims.quote: According to popular legend, they are a male and female pair: the female looking out to sea, watching for the seamen to return safely home, and the male looking in to the city, watching over the seamen's families

claims.statement: The birds face apart; if they mated and flew off the city would cease to exist.
claims.statement_id: Kedua burung saling membelakangi; jika kawin dan terbang, kota lenyap.
claims.quote: Local legend also holds that the birds face away from each other, for if they were to mate and fly away, the city would cease to exist.

claims.statement: Another legend (Legende): they are chained, as if they flew off the Mersey (Fluss Mersey) would flood Liverpool.
claims.statement_id: Legenda lain (Legende): dirantai, karena jika terbang Sungai Mersey (Fluss Mersey) meluap membanjiri Liverpool.
claims.quote: Eine andere Legende besagt, dass sie angekettet sind, weil der Fluss Mersey über die Ufer treten und die Stadt Liverpool überschwemmen würde, wenn sie wegfliegen.

claims.statement: The Liver Bird (Livervogel) is a mythological being (mythologisches Wesen) and symbol of the English (englischen) city of Liverpool.
claims.statement_id: Liver Bird (Livervogel) makhluk mitologis (mythologisches Wesen) lambang kota Inggris (englischen) Liverpool.
claims.quote: Der Liver Bird ( ˈlaɪvər bɜrd, dt. etwa: Livervogel) ist ein mythologisches Wesen und Symbolfigur der englischen Stadt Liverpool.

claims.statement: Llŷr (Welsh Llŷr Llediaith, half-speech) was likely a Welsh sea god, related to the Irish Ler, father of Manannán mac Lir; leader of the Children of Llyr against the Children of Dôn.
claims.statement_id: Llŷr (Wales, Welsh: Llŷr Llediaith, setengah bicara) kemungkinan dewa laut Wales, kerabat Ler Irlandia (Irish), ayah Manannán mac Lir; pemimpin Children of Llyr melawan Children of Dôn; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Lleddiaith meaning 'half-speech' or 'half-language') was likely a sea-god in Welsh mythology, related to the Irish Ler ('the Sea'), father of Manannán mac Lir. In some legends, he is the leader of the Children of Llyr, who are constantly at war with the Children of Dôn.

claims.statement: Llŷr is father of Brân, Brânwen and Manawydan by Penarddun in Branwen, Daughter of Llyr, the Second Branch of the Mabinogi.
claims.statement_id: Llŷr ayah Brân (Brân the Blessed), Brânwen (Branwen), Manawydan dari Penarddun dalam Branwen, Daughter of Llyr, Cabang Kedua (Second Branch) Mabinogi.
claims.quote: Llŷr appears as the father of Brân, Brânwen and Manawydan by Penarddun in the Branwen, Daughter of Llyr, the Second Branch of the Mabinogi.

claims.statement: The Welsh Triads: Llŷr imprisoned by Euroswydd; Penarddun bore Nisien and Efnisien.
claims.statement_id: Welsh Triads: Llŷr dipenjarakan Euroswydd; Penarddun melahirkan Nisien dan Efnisien.
claims.quote: The Welsh Triads states that Llŷr was imprisoned by Euroswydd, and presumably, Penarddun subsequently married Euroswydd, giving birth by Euroswydd to her two younger sons, Nisien and Efnisien, as stated in the Second Branch.

claims.statement: Shakespeare's King Lear comes from Geoffrey of Monmouth's King Leir, often linked to but likely unrelated to Llŷr.
claims.statement_id: King Lear (William Shakespeare) dari King Leir karya Geoffrey of Monmouth, sering dikaitkan dengan Llŷr tetapi kemungkinan tak berhubungan.
claims.quote: William Shakespeare's play King Lear is based on material taken secondhand (through Raphael Holinshed) from Geoffrey of Monmouth's mythical king King Leir, who has often been connected, but is likely unrelated, to Llŷr.

claims.statement: Llŷr is the Welsh counterpart (walisische Pendant) of the Irish sea god (irischen Meeresgott) Lir; llyr means sea.
claims.statement_id: Llŷr padanan Wales (walisische Pendant) dewa laut Irlandia (irischen Meeresgott) Lir; llyr berarti laut.
claims.quote: ist das walisische Pendant zum irischen Meeresgott Lir.

claims.statement: Llŷr and Lir have a bird affinity (Vogelsympathie); Llŷr's children's names carry raven symbolism (Rabensymbolik).
claims.statement_id: Llŷr dan Lir punya kedekatan dengan burung (Vogelsympathie); nama anak Llŷr memuat lambang gagak (Rabensymbolik).
claims.quote: Sowohl der walisische Llŷr als auch der irische Lir haben offenbar eine Vogelsympathie. Llŷrs Kinder tragen im Namen eine Rabensymbolik

claims.statement: Llŷr Lledieith, with Gweir fab Geirioedd and Mabon fab Modron, is one of the three exalted prisoners of the Isle of Britain (Insel Britannien).
claims.statement_id: Llŷr Lledieith, bersama Gweir fab Geirioedd dan Mabon fab Modron, salah satu tiga tahanan agung Pulau Britania (Insel Britannien).
claims.quote: Llŷr Lledieith wird zusammen mit Gweir fab Geirioedd und Mabon fab Modron „Einer der drei erhabenen Gefangenen der Insel Britannien“

claims.statement: The redcap (powrie) is a murderous goblin of the Anglo-Scottish border, haunting ruined castles and soaking its cap in blood; also Redcomb, Bloody Cap.
claims.statement_id: Redcap (powrie) goblin pembunuh perbatasan Inggris-Skotlandia (Anglo-Scottish), menghuni kastel runtuh, merendam topi dalam darah; juga Redcomb, Bloody Cap; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: The redcap (or powrie) is a type of malevolent, murderous goblin found in folklore of the Anglo-Scottish border region. The redcap is said to inhabit ruined castles along the Anglo-Scottish border, especially those that were the scenes of tyranny or wicked deeds, and is known for soaking his cap in the blood of his victims. He is also known as Redcomb and Bloody Cap.

claims.statement: A short old elf with long teeth, eagle talons, red eyes, iron boots, pikestaff and red cap.
claims.statement_id: Elf tua pendek, gigi panjang, cakar elang, mata merah, sepatu besi, tongkat tombak, topi merah.
claims.quote: Redcap is depicted as "a short, thickset old elf with long prominent teeth, skinny fingers armed with talons like eagles, large eyes of a fiery red colour, grisly hair streaming down his shoulders, iron boots, a pikestaff in his left hand, and a red cap on his head".

claims.statement: It hurls stones at travellers and soaks its cap in their blood.
claims.statement_id: Ia melempar batu besar pada pelancong dan merendam topi dalam darah mereka.
claims.quote: When travellers take refuge in his lair, he flings huge stones at them and if he kills them, he soaks his cap in their blood, giving it a crimson hue.

claims.statement: Driven off by Scripture or a crucifix, vanishing in flames and leaving a large tooth.
claims.statement_id: Diusir dengan Kitab Suci (Scripture) atau salib, lenyap dalam api meninggalkan gigi besar.
claims.quote: He is unaffected by human strength, but can be driven away by words of Scripture or by the brandishing of a crucifix, which cause him to utter a dismal yell and vanish in flames, leaving behind a large tooth.

claims.statement: Scottish nobleman William de Soulis had a redcap familiar, Robin Redcap.
claims.statement_id: William de Soulis (bangsawan Skotlandia, Scottish) punya redcap bernama Robin Redcap.
claims.quote: Scottish nobleman William de Soulis was said in folklore to have a redcap familiar called "Robin Redcap".

claims.statement: The Redcap (Powrie, Dunter) of British (britischen) folklore is a bloodthirsty goblin, kobold, elf or fairy (Fee).
claims.statement_id: Redcap (Powrie, Dunter) dalam folklore Britania (britischen) goblin haus darah, kobold, elf, atau peri (Fee).
claims.quote: Ein Red Cap oder Redcap (auch Powrie oder Dunter) ist in der britischen Folklore eine Art böswilliger blutrünstiger Goblin, Kobold, Elf oder auch Fee.

claims.statement: Redcaps must find victims regularly, as they die when the blood in their caps (Mützen) dries.
claims.statement_id: Redcap harus terus mencari korban karena mati bila darah di topinya (Mützen) kering.
claims.quote: Redcaps müssen regelmäßig Opfer finden, da sie sterben, sobald das Blut in ihren Mützen austrocknet.

claims.statement: Robin Redcap wrought harm on his master's home, Hermitage Castle.
claims.statement_id: Robin Redcap merusak kediaman tuannya, Hermitage Castle.
claims.quote: Er richtete viel Schaden an und zerstörte den Wohnsitz seines Herrn, Hermitage Castle.

claims.statement: Twrch Trwyth (Welsh Trwyd) is a boar of Arthurian legend; in Culhwch and Olwen (c. 1100) hunted by King Arthur and his hound Cafall (Cavall); tasks set by the giant Ysbaddaden.
claims.statement_id: Twrch Trwyth (Trwyd, Wales/Welsh) babi hutan legenda Arthurian; dalam Culhwch and Olwen (sekitar 1100) diburu Raja Arthur (King Arthur) dan anjing Cafall (Cavall); tugas raksasa Ysbaddaden.
claims.quote: is a fabulous wild boar in Arthurian legend. A richly elaborate account of its hunt is described in the Welsh prose romance Culhwch and Olwen, which was probably written around 1100. Its hunt involved King Arthur and his hosts and his hound Cafall

claims.statement: The boar was brought from Ireland to Britain and shoved into the sea at Cornwall.
claims.statement_id: Babi dibawa dari Irlandia (Ireland) ke Britania (Britain), didorong ke laut di Cornwall.
claims.quote: The boar was brought out of Ireland, driven to Britain, and finally shoved off a cliff into the sea at Cornwall.

claims.statement: Earliest mention in Gwarchan Cynfelyn (7th century), Book of Aneirin.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan tertua dalam Gwarchan Cynfelyn (abad ke-7), Book of Aneirin.
claims.quote: A passing reference in the elegy Gwarchan Cynfelyn (7th century), preserved in the Book of Aneirin, is reckoned to be its earliest mention in literature.

claims.statement: Historia Brittonum (Mirabilia): Arthur hunted the boar Troynt with his dog Cabal (Cavall).
claims.statement_id: Historia Brittonum (Mirabilia): Arthur memburu babi Troynt dengan anjing Cabal (Cavall).
claims.quote: It claims that Arthur was chasing the great boar Troynt [recte Troit] assisted by his dog Cabal, and the dog left its pawprint in rock

claims.statement: The name means the boar Trwyth, likened to the Irish boar Triath.
claims.statement_id: Nama berarti babi Trwyth, dianggap padanan babi Triath mitologi Irlandia (Irish).
claims.quote: The name in Welsh can be construed to mean "the boar Trwyth", and past scholars argued it may be analogous to the boar Triath of Irish mythology

claims.statement: The most famous boars (Eber) of Wales are Ysgithyrwyn and Twrch Trwyth with his sons.
claims.statement_id: Babi hutan (Eber) paling terkenal di Wales: Ysgithyrwyn dan Twrch Trwyth dengan putra-putranya.
claims.quote: Die bekanntesten Eber von Wales sind der Ysgithyrwyn und der Twrch Trwyth mit seinen Söhnen.

claims.statement: Pigs (Schweine) were the Celts' (Kelten) most important livestock.
claims.statement_id: Babi (Schweine) hewan ternak terpenting bangsa Kelt (Kelten).
claims.quote: Schweine waren die wichtigsten Haustiere der Kelten

claims.statement: The Brown Lady of Raynham Hall is a ghost of Raynham Hall, Norfolk, England, famous in the United Kingdom via a Country Life photograph; named for her brown brocade dress.
claims.statement_id: Brown Lady of Raynham Hall hantu Raynham Hall, Norfolk, Inggris (England); terkenal di Britania Raya (United Kingdom) lewat foto Country Life; nama dari gaun brokat cokelat.
claims.quote: The Brown Lady of Raynham Hall is a ghost that reportedly haunts Raynham Hall in Norfolk, England. It became one of the most famous hauntings in the United Kingdom when photographers from Country Life magazine claimed to have captured its image. The "Brown Lady" is so named because of the brown brocade dress it is claimed she wears.

claims.statement: Legend says the ghost is Dorothy Walpole (1686–1726), sister of Robert Walpole, first Prime Minister of Great Britain.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda hantu itu Dorothy Walpole (1686–1726), saudari Robert Walpole, Perdana Menteri pertama (first Prime Minister) Britania Raya (Great Britain).
claims.quote: According to legend, the apparition is that of Dorothy Walpole (1686–1726), the sister of Robert Walpole, generally regarded as the first Prime Minister of Great Britain.

claims.statement: Charles Townshend locked her in Raynham Hall for adultery with Lord Wharton.
claims.statement_id: Charles Townshend mengurungnya di Raynham Hall karena berselingkuh dengan Lord Wharton.
claims.quote: The story says that when Townshend discovered that his wife had committed adultery with Lord Wharton, he punished her by locking her in her rooms in the family home, Raynham Hall.

claims.statement: Lucia C. Stone: at Christmas 1835 Colonel Loftus and Hawkins saw the Brown Lady; Loftus noted her empty eye sockets.
claims.statement_id: Lucia C. Stone: Natal 1835, Kolonel Loftus dan Hawkins melihat Brown Lady; Loftus melihat rongga mata kosong.
claims.quote: Loftus and another guest named Hawkins said they had seen the "Brown Lady" one night as they approached their bedrooms, noting in particular the dated brown dress she wore. The following evening Loftus claimed to have seen the "Brown Lady" again, later reporting that on this occasion he was drawn to the spectre's empty eye-sockets

claims.statement: An 1836 sighting by Captain Frederick Marryat, friend of Charles Dickens.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan 1836 oleh Kapten (Captain) Frederick Marryat, sahabat Charles Dickens.
claims.quote: The next reported sighting of the "Brown Lady" was made in 1836 by Captain Frederick Marryat, a friend of novelist Charles Dickens, and the author of a series of popular sea novels.

claims.statement: No proof the photo (1936, Country Life) is genuine; sceptics such as Joe Nickell think it faked, perhaps by multiple exposure (Mehrfachbelichtung).
claims.statement_id: Tak ada bukti keaslian foto (1936, Country Life); ilmuwan skeptis seperti Joe Nickell menganggapnya palsu, mungkin pencahayaan ganda (Mehrfachbelichtung).
claims.quote: Beweise für die Echtheit des Fotos oder weiterer Sichtungen gibt es nicht. Heutige skeptische Wissenschaftler, darunter Joe Nickell, gehen davon aus, dass das Bild gefälscht ist, möglicherweise durch Mehrfachbelichtung.

claims.statement: First recorded sighting by Lucia C. Stone at Christmas 1835 at Raynham Hall.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan pertama tercatat oleh Lucia C. Stone pada Natal 1835 di Raynham Hall.
claims.quote: The first recorded claim of a sighting of the ghost was by Lucia C. Stone concerning a gathering at Raynham Hall in the Christmas of 1835.

claims.statement: Crom Cruach (Old Irish Cromm Crúaich) was a pagan god of pre-Christian Ireland; per Christian writers, appeased by human sacrifice, ended by Saint Patrick; also Crom Cróich, Cenn Cruach, Cenncroithi; related to Crom Dubh.
claims.statement_id: Crom Cruach (Irlandia Kuno/Old Irish Cromm Crúaich) dewa pagan Irlandia (Ireland) pra-Kristen; penulis Kristen (Christian): kurban manusia, diakhiri Santo Patrick (Saint Patrick); juga Crom Cróich, Cenn Cruach, Cenncroithi; terkait Crom Dubh.
claims.quote: was a pagan god of pre-Christian Ireland. According to Christian writers, he was propitiated with human sacrifice and his worship was ended by Saint Patrick. He is also referred to as Crom Cróich, Cenn Cruach/Cróich ([kʲen̪ː ˈkɾuːa̯x] ) and Cenncroithi ([kʲen̪ː ˈkɾoθʲi] ). He is related to the later mythological and folkloric figure Crom Dubh.

claims.statement: A 12th-century dinnsenchas poem: sacrifice for milk and grain, a fertility god; a gold figure with twelve others, the sun and zodiac.
claims.statement_id: Puisi dinnsenchas abad ke-12: kurban demi susu dan gandum, dewa kesuburan; sosok emas dengan dua belas sosok, matahari dan zodiak.
claims.quote: The references in a dinnsenchas ("place-lore") poem in the 12th century to sacrifice in exchange for milk and grain suggest that Crom had a function as a fertility god. The description of his image as a gold figure surrounded by twelve stone or bronze figures has been interpreted by some as representing the sun surrounded by the signs of the zodiac

claims.statement: Book of Leinster: his idol on Magh Slécht in County Cavan received first-born sacrifice for milk and grain.
claims.statement_id: Book of Leinster: arca di Magh Slécht, County Cavan, kurban anak sulung demi susu dan gandum.
claims.quote: Crom Cruach's cult image, consisting of a gold figure surrounded by twelve stone figures, stood on Magh Slécht ("the plain of prostration") (pronounced Moy Shlokht) in County Cavan, and was propitiated with first-born sacrifice in exchange for good yields of milk and grain.

claims.statement: High King Tigernmas died worshipping him on Samhain eve; the idol was destroyed by St. Patrick with a sledgehammer.
claims.statement_id: Raja Agung (High King) Tigernmas mati saat memujanya pada malam Samhain; arca dihancurkan St. Patrick (Saint Patrick) dengan palu godam.
claims.quote: An early High King, Tigernmas, along with three quarters of his army, is said to have died while worshipping Crom on Samhain eve, but worship continued until the cult image was destroyed by St. Patrick with a sledgehammer.

claims.statement: Cromm Cruach is a god of the underworld and death (Gott der Unterwelt und des Todes) in Irish (irischen) tradition.
claims.statement_id: Cromm Cruach dewa dunia bawah dan kematian (Gott der Unterwelt und des Todes) dalam tradisi Irlandia (irischen).
claims.quote: ist ein angeblicher Gott der Unterwelt und des Todes in der irischen Überlieferung.

claims.statement: Sometimes merged with the fertility god (Fruchtbarkeitsgott) Cromm Dubh (Crom Dubh); also Cenn Crúach.
claims.statement_id: Kadang dicampur dengan dewa kesuburan (Fruchtbarkeitsgott) Cromm Dubh (Crom Dubh); juga Cenn Crúach.
claims.quote: Cromm Cruach wird manchmal mit dem Cromm Dubh (der „Schwarzer Gebeugte“) genannten Fruchtbarkeitsgott zusammengeworfen

issues.message: 1 kutipan tidak bisa dicek otomatis: www.gutenberg.org (tidak bisa dibuka (fetch failed)).

claims.statement: In Norse mythology the Dökkálfar (Dark Elves) and Ljósálfar (Light Elves) are two kinds of elves; dark in the earth, light in Álfheimr.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Nordik (Norse mythology), Dökkálfar (Dark Elves) dan Ljósálfar (Light Elves) dua jenis elf; elf gelap di dalam bumi, elf terang di Álfheimr.
claims.quote: In Norse mythology, Dökkálfar ("Dark Elves") and Ljósálfar ("Light Elves") are two contrasting types of elves; the dark elves dwell within the earth and have a dark complexion, while the light elves live in Álfheimr, and are "fairer than the sun to look at".

claims.statement: Attested in Snorri Sturluson's 13th-century Prose Edda and the Old Norse poem Hrafnagaldr Óðins.
claims.statement_id: Tercatat dalam Prose Edda karya Snorri Sturluson (abad ke-13) dan puisi Norse Kuno (Old Norse) Hrafnagaldr Óðins; di Islandia.
claims.quote: The Ljósálfar and the Dökkálfar are attested in the Prose Edda, written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson, and in the late Old Norse poem Hrafnagaldr Óðins.

claims.statement: In Gylfaginning ch. 17 High says the Ljósálfar live in Álfheimr, the Dökkálfar underground; light fairer than the sun, dark blacker than pitch.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 17 Gylfaginning, High: Ljósálfar di Álfheimr, Dökkálfar di bawah tanah; terang lebih elok dari matahari, gelap lebih hitam dari ter.
claims.quote: High says that the Ljósálfar live in Álfheimr, while the Dökkálfar dwell underground and look—and particularly behave—quite unlike the Ljósálfar. High describes the Ljósálfar as "fairer than the sun to look at", while the Dökkálfar are "blacker than pitch".

claims.statement: High: the other heavens (Andlàngr, Víðbláinn, Gimlé) are for now inhabited only by light elves.
claims.statement_id: High: langit lain (Andlàngr, Víðbláinn, Gimlé) untuk sementara hanya dihuni elf terang.
claims.quote: High adds that "we believe it is only light-elves who inhabit these places for the time being".

claims.statement: Anderson's translation (Younger Edda, Gutenberg): light-elves in Alfheim, dark-elves in the earth, unlike in appearance and deeds.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Anderson (Younger Edda, Gutenberg): elf terang di Alfheim, elf gelap di dalam bumi, berbeda rupa dan perbuatan.
claims.quote: There dwell the folk that are called light-elves; but the dark-elves dwell down in the earth, and they are unlike the light-elves in appearance, but much more so in deeds.

claims.statement: It is unclear whether the distinction originated with Snorri.
claims.statement_id: Tak jelas apakah pembedaan ini berasal dari Snorri.
claims.quote: As the concept is only recorded in Gylfaginning and the late poem Hrafnagaldr Óðins, it is unclear whether the distinction between the two types of elves originated with Snorri, or if he was merely recounting a concept already developed.

claims.statement: Perhaps Christian influence, angels of light and darkness; Anne Holtsmark's view.
claims.statement_id: Mungkin pengaruh Kristen (Christian), malaikat terang dan gelap; pendapat Anne Holtsmark.
claims.quote: The sub-classification perhaps resulted from Christian influence, by way of importation of the concept of good and evil and angels of light and darkness. Anne Holtsmark aired this view, though with some reservation

claims.statement: The leannán sídhe (Irish, fairy lover; Scottish Gaelic leannan sìth; Manx lhiannan shee) is a Celtic figure, an Aos Sí woman taking a human lover.
claims.statement_id: Leannán sídhe (Irlandia/Irish, kekasih peri; Scottish Gaelic leannan sìth; Manx lhiannan shee) sosok mitologi Kelt (Celtic), perempuan Aos Sí yang mengambil kekasih manusia; di Irlandia. (Skotlandia)
claims.quote: is a figure from Celtic mythology. She is depicted as a beautiful woman of the Aos Sí ("people of the fairy mounds") who takes a human lover. Lovers of the leannán sídhe are said to live brief, though highly inspired, lives.

claims.statement: There is a reference to a male leannán sídhe; the name is from Gaelic words for lover.
claims.statement_id: Ada rujukan leannán sídhe laki-laki; nama dari kata Gaelik (Gaelic) untuk kekasih.
claims.quote: While the leannán sídhe is most often depicted as a female fairy, there is at least one reference to a male leannán sídhe troubling a mortal woman.

claims.statement: Popularised in the Celtic Revival; Jane Wilde (Speranza), Ancient Legends, Mystic Charms and Superstitions of Ireland (1887).
claims.statement_id: Dipopulerkan saat Kebangkitan Kelt (Celtic Revival); Jane Wilde (Speranza), Ancient Legends, Mystic Charms and Superstitions of Ireland (1887).
claims.quote: A version of the myth was popularized during the Celtic Revival in the late 19th-century. The leannán sídhe is mentioned by Jane Wilde, writing as "Speranza", in her 1887 Ancient Legends, Mystic Charms and Superstitions of Ireland.

claims.statement: W. B. Yeats: a near-vampiric beautiful muse giving inspiration for love, ending in madness and death.
claims.statement_id: W. B. Yeats: muse cantik yang hampir vampirik, memberi ilham demi cinta, berujung kegilaan dan kematian.
claims.quote: W. B. Yeats popularized his own 'newly-ancient' version of the leannán sídhe, emphasizing the spirit's almost vampiric tendencies. As he imagined it, the leannán sídhe is depicted as a beautiful muse who offers inspiration to an artist in exchange for their love and devotion; although the supernatural affair leads to madness and eventual death for the artist

claims.statement: Similarly the Lhiannan Shee known on the Isle of Man.
claims.statement_id: Serupa Lhiannan Shee di Isle of Man.
claims.quote: Ähnlich gestaltet es sich bei der Lhiannan Shee, die auf der Isle of Man bekannt ist.

claims.statement: The fairies (Feen) use up their lovers' lives and do not let them escape even after death.
claims.statement_id: Para peri (Feen) menghabiskan nyawa kekasihnya dan tak membiarkan mereka lolos setelah mati.
claims.quote: Die Feen brauchen das Leben ihrer Liebhaber auf und lassen sie auch nach dem Tod nicht entkommen.

claims.statement: Gaelic poets die young, for she is restless (per W. B. Yeats).
claims.statement_id: Penyair Gaelik (Gaelic) mati muda karena ia gelisah (menurut W. B. Yeats).
claims.quote: The Gaelic poets die young, for she is restless, and will not let them remain long on earth—this malignant phantom.

claims.statement: Nabia (Navia) was a goddess of the Pre-Roman peoples of the Iberian Peninsula, also worshipped under Roman occupation.
claims.statement_id: Nabia (Navia) dewi bangsa pra-Romawi (Pre-Roman) Semenanjung Iberia (Iberian Peninsula), dipuja juga masa Romawi (Roman).
claims.quote: Nabia (or Navia) was a goddess of the Pre-Roman peoples of the Iberian Peninsula, although she also had an extended cult during the Roman occupation of the peninsula.

claims.statement: Some historians suggest Nabia was a common word for deities; others question this.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sejarawan menduga Nabia kata umum untuk dewa; teori ini dipertanyakan.
claims.quote: Nabia was worshipped in many places on the Iberian Peninsula, sometimes in very different ways, leading some historians to suggest that "Nabia" was just a common word used by different peoples to refer to their deities (a theory questioned by others).

claims.statement: Read as a goddess of water, valleys, forests, hills, fertility, health and abundance; 28 inscriptions as of 2025.
claims.statement_id: Ditafsirkan dewi air, lembah, hutan, bukit, kesuburan, kesehatan, kelimpahan; 28 prasasti hingga 2025.
claims.quote: Due to the uncertainty of her nature, she is sometimes interpreted as a water deity, other times she is associated with valleys, forests and hills, and she's further seen as the goddess of fertility, health, and abundance. Her name, including variations, is attested in 28 inscriptions as of 2025.

claims.statement: Nabia (Navia) was the goddess of rivers and water (déesse des rivières et de l'eau) in Luso-Galician myth, in Galicia (Galice), Asturias (Asturies), Spain (Espagne) and Portugal.
claims.statement_id: Nabia (Navia) dewi sungai dan air (déesse des rivières et de l'eau) mitologi Luso-Galicia, di Galicia (Galice), Asturias (Asturies), Spanyol (Espagne), dan Portugal.
claims.quote: Nabia ou Navia était la déesse des rivières et de l'eau dans la mythologie luso-galiciennes, sur le territoire de la Galice moderne (Espagne), des Asturies (Espagne) et du Portugal.

claims.statement: Twenty inscriptions among the Gallaeci (Galiciens) and Lusitanians (Lusitaniens); a pre-Celtic Indo-European fertility goddess.
claims.statement_id: Dua puluh prasasti di wilayah Galicia (Galiciens) dan Lusitania (Lusitaniens); dewi pra-Kelt asal Indo-Eropa, dewi kesuburan.
claims.quote: Elle est l'une des divinités les plus observées, avec vingt épigraphes documentant leur culte dans une région qui comprend des Galiciens et des Lusitaniens. De genre féminin, cette divinité pré-celtique d'origine indo-européenne est généralement considérée comme une déesse de la fertilité.

claims.statement: The rivers Navia and Avia in Galicia and Asturias, and the Neiva near Braga.
claims.statement_id: Sungai Navia dan Avia di Galicia dan Asturias, serta Neiva dekat Braga.
claims.quote: Les rivières actuelles de Navia et d'Avia, en Galice et aux Asturies, le fleuve Neiva, près de Braga

claims.statement: Diana, the Roman goddess often compared to Nabia.
claims.statement_id: Diana, dewi Romawi (Roman) yang sering dibandingkan dengan Nabia.
claims.quote: Diana, the Roman goddess often compared to Nabia.

claims.statement: The Fontaine de l'Idole (Fonte do Ídolo) at Braga; main function goddess of rivers and water.
claims.statement_id: Fontaine de l'Idole (Fonte do Ídolo) di Braga; fungsi utama dewi sungai dan air.
claims.quote: La Fontaine de l'Idole à Braga Caractéristiques Fonction principale déesse des rivières et de l'eau

claims.statement: Nabia is a goddess of Celtic mythology (mythologie celtique).
claims.statement_id: Nabia dewi mitologi Kelt (mythologie celtique).
claims.quote: Nabia Déesse de la mythologie celtique

claims.statement: The spriggan is a legendary creature of Cornish folklore, especially West Penwith.
claims.statement_id: Spriggan makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish folklore), terutama West Penwith; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: A spriggan /sprɪdʒən/ is a legendary creature from Cornish folklore. Spriggans are particularly associated with West Penwith in Cornwall.
