claims.statement: From the Cornish plural spyrysyon, spirits.
claims.statement_id: Dari jamak bahasa Cornwall (Cornish) spyrysyon, roh.
claims.quote: Spriggan is pronounced /sprɪdʒən/ rather than /sprɪɡən/; the word is borrowed from the Cornish plural spyrysyon 'spirits'.

claims.statement: They guard treasure at ruins and barrows; ghosts of giants with giant strength; per Robert Hunt able to swell.
claims.statement_id: Menjaga harta di reruntuhan dan gundukan; hantu raksasa berkekuatan raksasa; menurut Robert Hunt dapat membengkak.
claims.quote: They were said to be found at old ruins, cairns, and barrows guarding buried treasure. Although small in stature, they have often been considered to be the ghosts of giants and retained gigantic strength, and in one story collected by Robert Hunt, they showed the ability to swell to enormous size.

claims.statement: They raised whirlwinds, sent storms to blight crops and stole children, leaving changelings.
claims.statement_id: Menimbulkan angin puyuh, badai merusak tanaman, mencuri anak dan meninggalkan changeling.
claims.quote: They raised sudden whirlwinds to terrify travellers, sent storms to blight crops, and sometimes stole away mortal children, leaving their ugly changelings in their place.

claims.statement: An old woman beat spriggans by turning her clothing inside out.
claims.statement_id: Seorang nenek mengalahkan spriggan dengan membalik pakaiannya.
claims.quote: In one story, an old woman got the better of a band of spriggans by turning her clothing inside-out

claims.statement: Katharine Briggs (from Robert Hunt and William Bottrell): fairy bodyguards; English Dialect Dictionary (1905): like Scandinavian trolls.
claims.statement_id: Katharine Briggs (dari Robert Hunt, William Bottrell): pengawal peri; English Dialect Dictionary (1905): seperti troll Skandinavia (Scandinavia).
claims.quote: Based on the collections of Robert Hunt and William Bottrell, Katharine Briggs characterized the spriggans as fairy bodyguards. The English Dialect Dictionary (1905) compared them to the trolls of Scandinavia.

claims.statement: In Cornish folk belief (kornischen Volksglauben) spriggans are called thieves (Diebe), robbers (Räuber) and villains (Schurken).
claims.statement_id: Spriggan dalam kepercayaan rakyat Cornwall (kornischen Volksglauben) disebut pencuri (Diebe), perampok (Räuber), penjahat (Schurken).
claims.quote: Spriggans sind im kornischen Volksglauben Fabelwesen, die man als üble Diebe, Räuber, Einbrecher und Schurken bezeichnet.

claims.statement: Hunt linked these spirits with the hillfort of Trencrom Hill.
claims.statement_id: Hunt mengaitkan spriggan dengan benteng bukit Trencrom Hill.
claims.quote: Hunt associated these spirits with the hillfort known as Trencrom Hill in Cornwall.

claims.statement: In Scottish folklore Am Fear Liath Mòr (Scottish Gaelic, Big Grey Man; Big Grey Man of Ben Macdui, Greyman) is a cryptid of Ben Macdui in the Cairngorms, second highest in the British Isles after Ben Nevis.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), Am Fear Liath Mòr (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic, Lelaki Kelabu Besar; Big Grey Man of Ben Macdui, Greyman) kriptid di Ben Macdui, Cairngorms, kedua tertinggi di Kepulauan Britania (British Isles) setelah Ben Nevis; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is the name for a presence or cryptid which is said to haunt the summit and passes of Ben Macdui, the highest peak of the Cairngorms and the second highest peak in the British Isles after Ben Nevis.

claims.statement: Very thin, over three metres tall, dark skin and hair, long arms, broad shoulders.
claims.statement_id: Sangat kurus, lebih dari tiga meter, kulit dan rambut gelap, lengan panjang, bahu lebar.
claims.quote: It is said to be very thin and over ten feet (three metres) tall, with dark skin and hair, long arms, and broad shoulders.

claims.statement: Usually unseen in fog; only crunching gravel and unease.
claims.statement_id: Biasanya tak terlihat dalam kabut; hanya bunyi kerikil berderak dan rasa gelisah.
claims.quote: Most often, the creature remains unseen in the fog of the mountain, with encounters limited to the sound of crunching gravel as it walks behind climbers and a general feeling of unease around the mountain.

claims.statement: Similar to the Brenin Llwyd (Grey King) of Welsh mythology.
claims.statement_id: Mirip Brenin Llwyd (Raja Kelabu, Grey King) mitologi Wales (Welsh).
claims.quote: The figure has many similarities with the Brenin Llwyd (English: Grey King ) of Welsh mythology, this figure is also semi-corporeal, silent and uses the mists as a cloak to prey on unwary travellers.

claims.statement: 1925: J. Norman Collie (Royal Geographical Society) told of an 1891 experience on Ben Macdui; crunching steps in the mist.
claims.statement_id: 1925: J. Norman Collie (Royal Geographical Society) menceritakan pengalaman 1891 di Ben Macdui; langkah berderak dalam kabut.
claims.quote: In 1925, J. Norman Collie gave the first recorded account of a Grey Man encounter. A noted hiker, professor, and member of the Royal Geographical Society, Collie recounted a terrifying experience he had as he hiked alone near the summit of Ben Macdui years earlier in 1891.

claims.statement: In Scottish (schottischen) tradition a supernatural phenomenon; compared with the Himalayan Yeti and North America's (Nordamerikas) Bigfoot.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Skotlandia (schottischen) fenomena gaib; dibandingkan dengan Yeti Himalaya dan Bigfoot Amerika Utara (Nordamerikas).
claims.quote: In der schottischen Tradition wird er als übernatürliches Phänomen betrachtet, daneben gibt es jedoch gelegentlich auch Vergleiche mit dem Yeti des Himalaya und dem Bigfoot Nordamerikas.

claims.statement: Am Fear Liath Mòr is a cryptid (Kryptiden) around Ben Macdui in Scotland (schottische), between Banffshire and Aberdeenshire.
claims.statement_id: Am Fear Liath Mòr kriptid (Kryptiden) di sekitar Ben Macdui, Skotlandia (schottische), antara Banffshire dan Aberdeenshire.
claims.quote: ist der Name eines Kryptiden, der in der Region um das schottische Ben Macdui zwischen dem Banffshire und Aberdeenshire leben soll.

claims.statement: In British folklore, British big cats are reported sightings of non-native wild big cats in the United Kingdom: panthers, pumas, black cats.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Britania (British folklore), British big cats: penampakan kucing besar liar non-asli di Britania Raya (United Kingdom), panther, puma, black cats.
claims.quote: In British folklore and urban legend, British big cats refers to the subject of reported sightings of non-native, wild big cats in the United Kingdom. Many of these creatures have been described as "panthers", "pumas", or "black cats".

claims.statement: Eurasian lynx recovered; a puma captured in 1980 in Scotland; thought escaped or released illegal exotic pets.
claims.statement_id: Lynx Eurasia (Eurasian lynx) ditemukan; puma tertangkap 1980 di Skotlandia (Scotland); diduga peliharaan eksotis ilegal yang kabur atau dilepas.
claims.quote: There have been rare isolated incidents of recovered individual animals, often medium-sized species like the Eurasian lynx, although in one 1980 case, a puma was captured alive in Scotland. These are generally believed to have been escaped or released exotic pets that were held illegally

claims.statement: A population of true big cats is rejected by experts and the British government.
claims.statement_id: Populasi kucing besar sejati ditolak ahli dan pemerintah Britania (British government).
claims.quote: The existence of a population of "true big cats" in Britain, however, especially a breeding population, has been rejected by experts and the British government owing to a lack of convincing evidence for the presence of such animals.

claims.statement: One folklorist called them a media artifact.
claims.statement_id: Seorang folklorist menyebutnya artefak media.
claims.quote: One folklorist considered such sightings of creatures to be a "media artifact" driven by British journalistic practices in the 1970s and 1980s

claims.statement: The Welsh poem Pa Gwr in the Black Book of Carmarthen: Cath Palug roamed Anglesey until slain by Cei.
claims.statement_id: Puisi Wales (Welsh) Pa Gwr dalam Black Book of Carmarthen: Cath Palug di Anglesey dibunuh Cei.
claims.quote: A medieval Welsh poem Pa Gwr in the Black Book of Carmarthen mentions a Cath Palug, meaning "Palug's cat" or "clawing cat", which roamed Anglesey until slain by Cei.

claims.statement: Their existence is unproven; theories: released after the Dangerous Wild Animals Act 1976, or surviving Ice Age (Edad de Hielo) fauna in Great Britain (Gran Bretaña).
claims.statement_id: Keberadaannya belum terbukti; teori: dilepas setelah Dangerous Wild Animals Act 1976 atau fauna sisa Zaman Es (Edad de Hielo); Britania Raya (Gran Bretaña).
claims.quote: Su existencia no ha sido comprobada, pero existen muchas teorías que intentan explicar cómo estos animales pudieron haber llegado a Gran Bretaña, incluyendo que son animales liberados después de que el Acta de animales salvajes peligrosos de 1976 entrara en vigor, o que son fauna superviviente de La Edad de Hielo.

claims.statement: This puma was caught in the woods of Inverness, Scotland (Escocia), in 1980, thought an abandoned pet.
claims.statement_id: Puma ditangkap di hutan Inverness, Skotlandia (Escocia), 1980, diduga peliharaan terlantar.
claims.quote: Este puma fue capturado en los bosques del condado de Inverness, Escocia en 1980. Se cree era una mascota abandonada.

claims.statement: Jenny Greenteeth (Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth, Grinteeth) is an English folklore river-hag like Peg Powler, from the grindylow, drowning children and the elderly.
claims.statement_id: Jenny Greenteeth (Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth, Grinteeth) sosok cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), nenek sihir sungai mirip Peg Powler, dari grindylow (Grindylow), menenggelamkan anak dan orang tua; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Jenny Greenteeth a.k.a. Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth and Grinteeth is a figure in English folklore. A river-hag, similar to Peg Powler and derived from the grindylow, she would pull children or the elderly into the water and drown them.

claims.statement: The name is also used for duckweed covering ponds; common around Liverpool and southwest Lancashire.
claims.statement_id: Nama juga untuk duckweed yang menutupi kolam; umum di Liverpool dan Lancashire barat daya.
claims.quote: The name is also used to describe pondweed or duckweed, which can form a continuous mat over the surface of a small body of water, making it misleading and potentially treacherous, especially to unwary children. With this meaning the name is common around Liverpool and southwest Lancashire.

claims.statement: Green-skinned, long-haired, sharp-toothed; Jinny Greenteeth in Lancashire and Staffordshire; Wicked Jenny, Ginny, Jeannie Greenteeth in Cheshire and Shropshire.
claims.statement_id: Berkulit hijau, berambut panjang, bergigi tajam; Jinny Greenteeth di Lancashire dan Staffordshire; Wicked Jenny, Ginny, Jeannie Greenteeth di Cheshire dan Shropshire.
claims.quote: Jenny Greenteeth was often described as green-skinned, with long hair, and sharp teeth. She is called Jinny Greenteeth in Lancashire and north Staffordshire but in Cheshire and Shropshire she is called Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth or Jeannie Greenteeth.

claims.statement: Her name derives from the Grindylow, also Grendith or Grinteeth.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari Grindylow, juga Grendith atau Grinteeth.
claims.quote: Her name is derived from that of the Grindylow which has the alternate name "Grendith" or "Grinteeth" which eventually developed into the term "Jenny Greenteeth".

claims.statement: Invented to frighten children, like the Slavic Rusalka, Japanese Kappa, Australia's Bunyip; some see sacrificial practices.
claims.statement_id: Diciptakan untuk menakuti anak, serupa Rusalka Slavia (Slavic), Kappa Jepang (Japanese), Bunyip Australia (Australia); sebagian folklorist: praktik kurban.
claims.quote: She is likely to have been an invention to frighten children from dangerous waters, similar in nature to the Slavic Rusalka, the Kappa in Japanese mythology, or Australia's Bunyip. Some folklorists believe the tale recalls sacrificial practices.

claims.statement: In Cheshire and Shropshire she is also called Peg o’ Nell.
claims.statement_id: Di Cheshire dan Shropshire juga disebut Peg o’ Nell.
claims.quote: In Lancashire wird sie Jinny Greenteeth, in Cheshire und Shropshire Ginny Greenteeth, Wicked Jenny oder Peg o’ Nell genannt.

claims.statement: In Breton folklore a Korrigan is a fairy or dwarf-like spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Breton (Breton folklore), Korrigan roh peri atau mirip kerdil; di Prancis.
claims.quote: In Breton folklore, a Korrigan ( pronounced [kɔˈriːɡãn] ) is a fairy or dwarf-like spirit.

claims.statement: Korrigan means small dwarf in Breton (korr dwarf, ig diminutive).
claims.statement_id: Korrigan berarti kerdil kecil dalam Breton (korr kerdil, ig pengecil).
claims.quote: The word korrigan means in Breton "small-dwarf" (korr means dwarf, ig is a diminutive and the suffix an is a hypocoristic).

claims.statement: Théodore de Villemarqué (Barzaz Breiz) uses it for fairy, distinct from dwarves.
claims.statement_id: Théodore de Villemarqué (Barzaz Breiz) memakainya setara peri, beda dari kerdil.
claims.quote: Théodore de Villemarqué in Barzaz Breiz uses the term interchangeably with "fairy" and distinguishes them from dwarves ("nains").

claims.statement: They give themselves away when they cannot list all the days of the week.
claims.statement_id: Mereka membuka kedok bila tak mampu menyebut seluruh hari dalam seminggu.
claims.quote: However, they give themselves away when they cannot enumerate the full list of the days of the week (because of the sacredness of the full week).

claims.statement: Siren-like female fairies of springs and rivers luring men to death; lovely at night, by day red-eyed, white-haired, wrinkled.
claims.statement_id: Peri perempuan mirip siren (Siren) di mata air dan sungai, memikat lelaki ke kematian; cantik malam, siang bermata merah, rambut putih, keriput.
claims.quote: Other authors use the term only to refer to siren-like female fairies who inhabit springs and rivers, "lovely lustful golden-haired women who tried to lure men into their beds – and into a watery death". These creatures are very beautiful when seen at dusk or night, but by day their eyes are red, their hair white, and their skin wrinkled

claims.statement: Princesses or druidesses opposed to Christianity in Brittany; they predict the future, change shape and move at lightning speed.
claims.statement_id: Putri atau druid perempuan yang menentang Kristen (Christianity) di Brittany (Apostles, Rasul; Virgin Mary); meramal, berubah wujud, cepat seperti kilat; mencuri anak, changeling (Changeling).
claims.quote: They are sometimes described as important princesses or druidesses who were opposed to Christianity when the Apostles came to convert Brittany. They hate priests, churches, and especially the Virgin Mary. They can predict the future, change shape, and move at lightning speed.

claims.statement: The Korriganen are fairies (Feen) or dwarf-like spectres (zwergenhafte Spukgestalten) of Celtic (keltischen) myth.
claims.statement_id: Korriganen peri (Feen) atau sosok hantu kerdil (zwergenhafte Spukgestalten) mitologi Kelt (keltischen).
claims.quote: Die Korriganen sind Feen oder zwergenhafte Spukgestalten aus der keltischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: They foresee the future, cure incurable illnesses (unheilbare Krankheiten), appear anywhere and take any shape.
claims.statement_id: Mereka meramal, menyembuhkan penyakit tak tersembuhkan (unheilbare Krankheiten), muncul di mana saja, berubah wujud.
claims.quote: Weiterhin werden ihnen magische Fähigkeiten nachgesagt: So sollen sie in die Zukunft blicken, unheilbare Krankheiten kurieren, jederzeit an jedem beliebigen Ort erscheinen und sogar jede beliebige Gestalt annehmen können.

claims.statement: Walter Evans-Wentz (The Fairy Faith in Celtic Countries): in Morbihan no clear distinction between korrigans and dwarves.
claims.statement_id: Walter Evans-Wentz (The Fairy Faith in Celtic Countries): di Morbihan tak ada beda jelas korrigan dan kerdil.
claims.quote: In contrast Walter Evans-Wentz in The Fairy Faith in Celtic Countries argued that in the mythology of Morbihan there is no clear distinction between korrigans and nains

claims.statement: Morag (Scottish Gaelic Mòrag) is a monster of Loch Morar, Scotland; after Nessie the most written about; a Scottish name punning on the loch.
claims.statement_id: Morag (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic Mòrag) monster Loch Morar, Skotlandia (Scotland); setelah Nessie paling banyak ditulis; nama perempuan Skotlandia (Scottish) sebagai permainan kata; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is the nickname given to a loch monster believed by many to live in Loch Morar, Scotland. After Nessie, it is among the most written about of Scotland's legendary monsters. "Morag", a Scottish female name, is a pun on the name of the loch.

claims.statement: Sightings since 1887, 34 by 1981, 16 with multiple witnesses.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan sejak 1887, 34 kejadian hingga 1981, 16 dengan banyak saksi.
claims.quote: Reported sightings date back to 1887, and numbered 34 incidents by 1981. Sixteen of these involved multiple witnesses.

claims.statement: August 1969: Duncan McDonell and William Simpson struck it; McDonell used an oar, Simpson fired a rifle; brown, 7.6–9.1 m, three humps.
claims.statement_id: Agustus 1969: Duncan McDonell dan William Simpson menabraknya, McDonell dengan dayung, Simpson menembak; cokelat, 7,6–9,1 m, tiga punuk.
claims.quote: A widely reported claim from August 1969 involved two local men, Duncan McDonell and William Simpson, and their boat, with which they claimed to have accidentally struck the creature, prompting it to attack them. McDonell defended with an oar, and Simpson opened fire with his rifle, whereupon it sank slowly out of sight.

claims.statement: Mhorag (Gaelic spirit of the loch), also Morag or Maggie, is a plesiosaur-like lake monster (plesiosaurierähnlichen Seeungeheuers) in Loch Morar, Scotland (Schottland).
claims.statement_id: Mhorag (roh danau, gälisch), juga Morag atau Maggie, monster danau mirip plesiosaurus (plesiosaurierähnlichen Seeungeheuers) di Loch Morar, Skotlandia (Schottland).
claims.quote: Mhorag [ ˈvɔrak] (gälisch: Geist des Sees), auch Morag oder Maggie, ist der Name eines plesiosaurierähnlichen Seeungeheuers, das angeblich im Loch Morar in Schottland leben soll.

claims.statement: 6–9 m long with humps (Höckern), very like the Loch Ness Monster (Ungeheuer von Loch Ness).
claims.statement_id: Panjang 6–9 m berpunuk (Höckern), mirip monster Loch Ness (Ungeheuer von Loch Ness, Loch Ness Monster).
claims.quote: Die Mhorag wird als sechs bis neun Meter langes Monster mit Höckern beschrieben und weist dadurch große Ähnlichkeit mit dem Ungeheuer von Loch Ness auf.

claims.statement: Mhorag has been observed about 30 times since January 1887.
claims.statement_id: Mhorag teramati sekitar 30 kali sejak Januari 1887.
claims.quote: Mhorag wurde seit Januar 1887 etwa 30 mal beobachtet

claims.statement: In Cornish folklore the Owlman (Cornish Kowanden; Cornish Owlman, Owlman of Mawnan) is an owl-like humanoid seen in 1976 at Mawnan, Cornwall, United Kingdom, flying over the church tower; perhaps a barn owl.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish folklore), Owlman (Cornish: Kowanden; Cornish Owlman, Owlman of Mawnan) humanoid mirip burung hantu, terlihat 1976 di Mawnan, Cornwall, Britania Raya (United Kingdom); terbang di atas menara gereja; mungkin burung hantu gudang.
claims.quote: In Cornish folklore, the Owlman (Cornish: Kowanden ), also known as the Cornish Owlman or Owlman of Mawnan, is an owl-like humanoid creature reportedly sighted in 1976 in the village of Mawnan, Cornwall, United Kingdom. The reported sightings of the creature flying above the local church tower have been interpreted by some as misidentifications of a barn owl

claims.statement: The story came from Tony Doc Shiels; two girls saw a winged creature above Mawnan church tower, 17 April 1976.
claims.statement_id: Kisah dari Tony Doc Shiels; dua gadis melihat makhluk bersayap di atas menara gereja Mawnan, 17 April 1976. Kowanden
claims.quote: The story originated with Tony "Doc" Shiels, who had been involved in a series of "monster-raising" exploits in 1976. Shiels claimed to have investigated a report of two young girls on holiday in Mawnan who allegedly saw a large winged creature hovering above the tower of St Mawnan and St Stephen's Church, Mawnan on 17 April 1976.

claims.statement: 3 July: Sally Chapman and Barbara Perry saw a big owl with pointed ears, as big as a man, glowing eyes, black claws.
claims.statement_id: 3 Juli: Sally Chapman dan Barbara Perry melihat burung hantu besar bertelinga runcing sebesar manusia, mata menyala, cakar hitam.
claims.quote: The account states that the two girls were camping when they encountered a creature described as a "big owl with pointed ears, as big as a man", with glowing eyes and black, pincer-like claws.

claims.statement: Sporadic sightings in 1978, 1979, 1989, 1995.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan sporadis 1978, 1979, 1989, 1995.
claims.quote: Sporadic reports of the Owlman sightings in the vicinity of the church were recorded in 1978, 1979, 1989, and 1995.

claims.statement: Gareth Medway: the story may have been a hoax by Shiels.
claims.statement_id: Gareth Medway: kisah itu mungkin tipuan Shiels.
claims.quote: Occult historian Gareth Medway suggested that the entire story may have been a hoax perpetrated by Shiels, who had a reputation for similar exploits.

claims.statement: In cryptozoological literature the Owlman is compared with the American cryptid Mothman (человеком-мотыльком). (America)
claims.statement_id: Dalam literatur kriptozoologi Owlman dibandingkan dengan kriptid Amerika Mothman (человеком-мотыльком). (America, Amerika)
claims.quote: Человека-сову в криптозоологической литературе иногда сравнивают с американским криптидом человеком-мотыльком.

claims.statement: Per Shiels, on 3 July two 14-year-old girls, Sally Chapman and Barbara Perry, encountered it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Shiels, 3 Juli dua gadis 14 tahun, Sally Chapman dan Barbara Perry, melihatnya.
claims.quote: According to Shiels, the Owlman was reportedly encountered again on 3 July by two 14-year-old girls, Sally Chapman and Barbara Perry, who were already familiar with the story.

claims.statement: The Questing Beast (Beast Glatisant; Old French beste glatisant; Modern French bête glatissante) is a composite Arthurian monster; in the French prose cycles and Le Morte d'Arthur hunted by King Pellinore, achieved by Sir Palamedes.
claims.statement_id: Questing Beast (Beast Glatisant; Prancis Kuno/Old French beste glatisant; Modern French bête glatissante) monster campuran dalam legenda Arthurian; siklus prosa Prancis (French), Le Morte d'Arthur; diburu Raja Pellinore (King Pellinore), dituntaskan Sir Palamedes; di Britania dan Prancis.
claims.quote: is a cross-animal monster appearing in many medieval texts of the Arthurian legend and modern works inspired by them. In the French prose cycles, and consequently in the quasi-canon of Le Morte d'Arthur, the hunt for the Beast is the subject of quests futilely undertaken by King Pellinore and his family, and finally achieved by Sir Palamedes and his companions.

claims.statement: Named for the noise from its belly; glatisant relates to French glapissant, yelping.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari bunyi keras dari perutnya; glatisant terkait kata Prancis (French) glapissant, menyalak.
claims.quote: Its name comes from the great noise that it emits from its belly (such motif seems to have originated in a symbolic dream scene in the Gesta Regum Anglorum). Glatisant is related to the French word glapissant, 'yelping' or 'barking', especially of small dogs or foxes.

claims.statement: Arthurian scholars see it as reflecting medieval views of giraffes (Camelopardalis).
claims.statement_id: Sarjana Arthurian: cerminan pandangan abad pertengahan tentang jerapah (Camelopardalis).
claims.quote: Arthurian scholars tend to interpret the beast as a reflection of the medieval mythological view on giraffes, whose generic name of Camelopardalis originated from their description of being half-camel and half-leopard.

claims.statement: In the Post-Vulgate, Merlin reveals it was born of a princess who lusted after her brother.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Post-Vulgate, Merlin: makhluk itu lahir dari putri yang bernafsu kepada saudaranya.
claims.quote: Merlin reveals that the monster had been born of a human woman, a princess who lusted after her own brother.

claims.statement: The brother foretold an abomination sounding like the dogs.
claims.statement_id: Saudara itu menubuatkan makhluk keji bersuara kawanan anjing.
claims.quote: Before he died, he prophesied that his sister would give birth to an abomination that would make the same sounds as the pack of dogs that were about to kill him.

claims.statement: The Glatisant (Questentier, bellendes Tier) is a bizarre creature of King Arthur's (König Artus) mythic world.
claims.statement_id: Glatisant (Questentier, bellendes Tier) makhluk aneh dunia mitos Raja Arthur (König Artus).
claims.quote: Das Glatisant, auch Questentier oder bellendes Tier genannt, ist eine bizarr anmutende Kreatur der mythischen Welt von König Artus

claims.statement: Serpent's head (Schlange), leopard's body (Leopard), lion's hindquarters (Löwen), deer's legs and hooves (Hirschs); baying like 30 hounds (Hunden).
claims.statement_id: Berkepala ular (Schlange), bertubuh macan tutul (Leopard), pantat singa (Löwen), kaki dan kuku rusa (Hirschs); gonggongan seperti 30 anjing (Hunden).
claims.quote: Es besitzt den Kopf einer Schlange und einen Körper wie ein Leopard, mit dem Hinterteil eines Löwen und Beinen und Hufen eines Hirschs. Aus seinem Inneren kommt ein tosender Lärm, ein Bellen wie von 30 Hunden in voller Hetze.

claims.statement: The hounds in its belly fall silent only when the Glatisant drinks.
claims.statement_id: Anjing di perutnya hanya diam saat Glatisant minum.
claims.quote: Wenn das Glatisant seinen gewaltigen Durst an einer Wasserstelle, normalerweise einem kühlen See oder Brunnen, stillt, dürfte das die einzige Gelegenheit sein, bei der die Hunde im Leib des Tieres einen Moment lang still verharren.

claims.statement: The water horse (waterhorse) is a mythical creature of Celtic and Nordic folklore: Welsh Ceffyl Dŵr, Irish each uisce, Scottish each-uisge and kelpie; a nixie's shape, Swedish bäckahästen, Faroese nykur.
claims.statement_id: Water horse (waterhorse) makhluk mitos cerita rakyat Kelt (Celtic) dan Nordik (Nordic folklore): Wales (Welsh) Ceffyl Dŵr, Irlandia (Irish) each uisce, Skotlandia (Scottish) each-uisge (Each-uisge) dan kelpie (Kelpie); wujud nixie (Nixie), Swedia (Swedish) bäckahästen (Bäckahästen), Faroe (Faroese) nykur; di Britania, Irlandia, Swedia, Faroe.
claims.quote: A water horse (also compounded as: waterhorse) is a mythical creature that appears in multiple forms in Celtic and Nordic folklore. Celtic incarnations includes: the Welsh Ceffyl Dŵr , Irish each uisce , the Scottish each-uisge and kelpie . In Nordic folklore, the water horse is a shape taken on by the nixie, in Swedish called bäckahästen ("the brook horse"), in Faroese nykur ("nixie").

claims.statement: Water horse was originally a name for the kelpie.
claims.statement_id: Water horse mulanya nama kelpie (Kelpie).
claims.quote: The term "water horse" was originally a name given to the kelpie, a creature similar to the hippocamp

claims.statement: A nickname for lake monsters such as Ogopogo and Nessie.
claims.statement_id: Julukan monster danau seperti Ogopogo dan Nessie.
claims.quote: The term has also been used as a nickname for lake monsters, particularly Ogopogo and Nessie.

claims.statement: Some see the terms as synonyms; others place the water horse in lochs and the kelpie in turbulent water.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian menganggap sinonim; lainnya: kuda air di danau (loch), kelpie di air deras.
claims.quote: some consider the two terms to be synonymous, while others distinguish the water horse as a denizen of lochs and the kelpie of turbulent water such as rivers, fords, and waterfalls.

claims.statement: The Wasserpferd is a fabulous being of many cultures, a water spirit (Wassergeistern), living in rivers, ponds, lakes or the sea.
claims.statement_id: Wasserpferd makhluk legenda dari berbagai budaya, roh air (Wassergeistern), hidup di sungai, kolam, danau, laut.
claims.quote: Ein Wasserpferd ist ein Fabelwesen, das aus verschiedenen Kulturen und Epochen bekannt ist und zu den Wassergeistern gezählt werden kann. Je nach Legende lebt es in Flüssen, Bächen, Teichen, Seen oder dem Meer.

claims.statement: Horses and water are linked in Denmark (Dänemark), Greece (Griechenland), Ireland (Irland) and Portugal; horse-shaped river spirits may stem from horse sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Kaitan kuda dan air dikenal di Denmark (Dänemark), Yunani (Griechenland), Irlandia (Irland), Portugal; roh sungai berwujud kuda mungkin dari kurban kuda.
claims.quote: Die Verbindung von Pferden mit Wasser ist aus Mythen und Legenden verschiedener Kulturen bekannt, zum Beispiel aus Dänemark, Griechenland, Irland und Portugal. Die Vorstellung von Flussgeistern in Pferdegestalt geht möglicherweise auf die historische Opferung von Pferden in Gewässern zurück.

claims.statement: The wild haggis (Haggis scoticus) is a fictional creature of Scottish folklore from the Scottish Highlands, jokingly the source of haggis.
claims.statement_id: Wild haggis (Haggis scoticus) makhluk rekaan cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highlands), sumber haggis secara bercanda; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Wild haggis (given the humorous taxonomic designation Haggis scoticus) is a fictional creature of Scottish folklore, said to be native to the Scottish Highlands. It is comically claimed to be the source of haggis, a traditional Scottish dish that is in fact made from the innards of sheep (including heart, lungs, and liver).

claims.statement: Its legs differ in length (like the sidehill gouger and dahu), running round mountains one way only.
claims.statement_id: Kaki kiri dan kanan berbeda panjang (seperti sidehill gouger dan dahu, Dahu, Sidehill gouger), berlari di gunung hanya satu arah.
claims.quote: According to some sources, the wild haggis's left and right legs are of different lengths (like the sidehill gouger and the dahu), allowing it to run quickly around the steep mountains and hillsides which make up its natural habitat, but only in one direction.

claims.statement: The two varieties cannot interbreed because the male loses his balance.
claims.statement_id: Dua varietas tak bisa kawin silang karena jantan kehilangan keseimbangan.
claims.quote: The two varieties coexist peacefully but are unable to interbreed in the wild because in order for the male of one variety to mate with a female of the other, he must turn to face in the same direction as his intended mate, causing him to lose his balance before he can mount her.

claims.statement: A 2003 Hall's of Broxburn survey: a third of U.S. visitors to Scotland believed it real.
claims.statement_id: Survei Hall's of Broxburn 2003: sepertiga pengunjung AS (U.S.) ke Skotlandia (Scotland) percaya ia nyata.
claims.quote: According to an online survey commissioned by haggis manufacturers Hall's of Broxburn, released on 26 November 2003, one-third of U.S. visitors to Scotland believed the wild haggis to be a real creature.

claims.statement: The Wildes Haggis (Haggis scoticus) is a fictional small mammal (fiktives kleines Säugetier) of Scottish (schottischen) folklore, said to live in the Highlands.
claims.statement_id: Wildes Haggis (Haggis scoticus) mamalia kecil rekaan (fiktives kleines Säugetier) folklore Skotlandia (schottischen), di Highlands.
claims.quote: Das Wilde Haggis (humoristischer wissenschaftlicher Name: Haggis scoticus) ist ein fiktives kleines Säugetier der schottischen Folklore, das angeblich in den Highlands beheimatet ist.

claims.statement: A small furry animal like a cross of rabbit (Kaninchen) and squirrel (Eichhörnchen), endemic to Scotland (Schottland).
claims.statement_id: Hewan kecil berbulu mirip persilangan kelinci (Kaninchen) dan tupai (Eichhörnchen), endemik Skotlandia (Schottland).
claims.quote: Das Wilde Haggis, eine in Schottland endemische Art, ist ein kleines, pelziges Tier, das einer Kreuzung aus Kaninchen und Eichhörnchen ähneln soll.

claims.statement: Two varieties: longer left or right legs, running clockwise or anticlockwise.
claims.statement_id: Dua varietas: kaki kiri atau kaki kanan lebih panjang, lari searah atau berlawanan jarum jam.
claims.quote: It is further claimed that there are two varieties of haggis, one with longer left legs and the other with longer right legs. The former variety can run clockwise around a mountain (as seen from above) while the latter can run anticlockwise.

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden Bencawr, Chief of Giants, is the antagonist of the Welsh Culhwch and Olwen, a vicious giant, father of Olwen and uncle of Goreu fab Custennin.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden Bencawr, Kepala Para Raksasa (hawthorn/mandul), antagonis Culhwch and Olwen (Wales, Welsh), raksasa kejam, ayah Olwen, paman Goreu fab Custennin; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Ysbaddaden Bencawr ; "Ysbaddaden, Chief of Giants" (from roots meaning "hawthorn" or "infertile" - or perhaps implying both meanings), is the primary antagonist of the Welsh romance Culhwch and Olwen. A vicious giant residing in a nigh unreachable castle, he is the father of Olwen and uncle of Goreu fab Custennin.

claims.statement: His stepmother curses Culhwch to marry only Olwen; he seeks Arthur.
claims.statement_id: Ibu tiri mengutuk Culhwch agar hanya menikahi Olwen; ia mencari Arthur.
claims.quote: Offended, the new queen puts a curse on him so that he can marry no one besides the beautiful Olwen, daughter of the giant Ysbaddaden.

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden took Custennin's lands and killed his twenty-three children.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden merampas tanah Custennin dan membunuh dua puluh tiga anaknya.
claims.quote: They learn that the castle belongs to Ysbaddaden, that he stripped Custennin of his lands and murdered the shepherd's twenty-three children out of cruelty.

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden tries to kill Culhwch with a poison dart, wounded by Bedwyr, Menw and Culhwch; sets impossible tasks (anoethau) including Twrch Trwyth.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden mencoba membunuh Culhwch dengan anak panah beracun, dilukai Bedwyr, Menw, Culhwch; memberi tugas mustahil (anoethau) termasuk Twrch Trwyth.
claims.quote: Upon their arrival, Ysbaddaden attempts to kill Culhwch with a poison dart, but is outwitted and wounded, first by Bedwyr, then by the enchanter Menw, and finally by Culhwch himself. Eventually, Ysbaddaden relents, and agrees to give Culhwch his daughter on the condition that he complete a number of impossible tasks (anoethau), including hunting the Twrch Trwy

claims.statement: Ysbaddaden Bencawr/Pengawyr in Welsh (walisischen) myth is a chief giant (Oberriese); his castle has nine gates (neun Toren); father of Olwen.
claims.statement_id: Ysbaddaden Bencawr/Pengawyr dalam mitologi Wales (walisischen) Oberriese, raksasa utama; kastel sembilan gerbang (neun Toren); ayah Olwen.
claims.quote: auch Ysbaddaden Pengawyr, ist in der walisischen Mythologie ein „Oberriese“ oder „Hauptriese“ (bencawr, pengawyr). Er besitzt eine Burg mit neun Toren und ist der Vater von Olwen, der Bruder des riesigen Schäfers Custenhin und der Onkel von Goreu.

claims.statement: His heavy eyelids (Augenlider) are lifted by a servant with a fork (Gabel); compare Balor.
claims.statement_id: Kelopak mata (Augenlider) berat diangkat pelayan dengan garpu (Gabel); bandingkan Balor.
claims.quote: Ysbaddaden hat Augenlider, die so schwer sind, dass sie ein Diener mit der Gabel hochheben muss, wenn er jemanden betrachten will (vergleiche dazu Balor).

claims.statement: Unexplained livestock deaths were blamed on creatures like the Beast of Bodmin Moor; British big cats.
claims.statement_id: Kematian hewan, terutama ternak, dituduhkan pada makhluk seperti Beast of Bodmin Moor; British big cats (kucing besar Britania).
claims.quote: unexplained animal deaths, typically livestock, would be blamed on such alleged creatures, like the Beast of Bodmin Moor and the Cotswolds Big Cat.

claims.statement: Per the ru article the Бодминский зверь is a big-cat-like animal seen over 60 times since 1983 on Bodmin Moor (Бодмин-Мур), Cornwall, England (Англия).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ru, Бодминский зверь hewan mirip kucing besar, terlihat lebih dari 60 kali sejak 1983 di Bodmin Moor (Бодмин-Мур), Cornwall, Inggris (Англия); kriptid; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Бодминский зверь — похожее на большую кошку животное, которое с 1983 года видели более 60 раз в местности Бодмин-Мур (Корнуолл, Англия).

claims.statement: A 1995 government inquiry found no evidence; sightings continued.
claims.statement_id: Penyelidikan pemerintah 1995 tak menemukan bukti; penampakan berlanjut.
claims.quote: Расследование, проведённое правительством в 1995 году, не выявило никаких свидетельств присутствия подобных животных, однако встречи с животным продолжались

claims.statement: A skull from the River Fowey given to the Natural History Museum came from a leopard skin rug.
claims.statement_id: Tengkorak dari River Fowey yang diserahkan ke Natural History Museum ternyata dari permadani kulit macan tutul.
claims.quote: In the case of the Beast of Bodmin, when a skull found in the River Fowey was presented to the Natural History Museum as proof of its existence, it was determined to have been cut from a leopard skin rug

claims.statement: The Bestia di Bodmin, a supposed big cat seen in Cornwall (Cornovaglia), Devon and Somerset; puma-like, dark grey to black.
claims.statement_id: Bestia di Bodmin, felin besar, terlihat di Cornwall (Cornovaglia), Devon, Somerset; mirip puma, abu-abu gelap hingga hitam.
claims.quote: La Bestia di Bodmin, nota anche come Bestia della Brughiera di Bodmin, è un presunto grosso felino; si dice che sia stato avvistato, appunto, nella Brughiera di Bodmin in Cornovaglia, ma anche in Devon e Somerset. Simile a un puma, dovrebbe essere di colore grigio scuro-nero

claims.statement: The skull (1995) belonged to a young male leopard, but it was not killed in England (Англии).
claims.statement_id: Tengkorak (1995) milik macan tutul jantan muda, tapi tak dibunuh di Inggris (Англии).
claims.quote: Сотрудники Музея естествознания, исследовавшие череп, определили, что он действительно принадлежал молодому самцу леопарда, однако было установлено, что животное не было убито в Англии

claims.statement: Scientists: such reports are usually unreliable; a population would need implausible numbers.
claims.statement_id: Ilmuwan: laporan semacam itu biasanya tak dapat dipercaya; populasi perlu jumlah tak masuk akal; iklim dan makanan menyulitkan.
claims.quote: Учёные указывают, что обычно сообщения о обнаружении подобных животных являются недостоверными, поскольку для поддержания их численности необходимо наличие неправдоподобно большого числа особей в популяции.

claims.statement: Damona was a goddess of Roman Gaul, known from Latin inscriptions; thermal-spring sanctuaries in Burgundy; a healing goddess; consort of Borvo.
claims.statement_id: Damona dewi Galia Romawi (Roman Gaul), prasasti Latin (Latin, Roman); tempat suci mata air panas di Burgundy; dewi penyembuh; pasangan Borvo; di Prancis.
claims.quote: Damona was a goddess worshipped in Roman Gaul, attested only by Latin votive inscriptions of the Roman period. The dedications come from the thermal-spring sanctuaries of eastern-central Gaul, chiefly in what is now Burgundy, where she was honoured as a healing goddess of the curative waters. She appears most often as the consort of the spring-god Borvo

claims.statement: Also paired with Albius and Apollo Moritasgus.
claims.statement_id: Juga berpasangan dengan Albius dan Apollo Moritasgus; Kelt.
claims.quote: but is also paired with the god Albius and with Apollo Moritasgus, and she is attested on her own.

claims.statement: The -ona ending as in Epona, Matrona, Sirona; the name from Celtic *damo-, cattle and deer.
claims.statement_id: Akhiran -ona seperti Epona, Matrona, Sirona; nama dari Kelt (Celtic) *damo-, lembu dan rusa.
claims.quote: The final element -ona is a common theonymic suffix that recurs in Gaulish divine names, as in Epona, Matrona, Sirona and Nemetona.

claims.statement: A Gaulish goddess of healing springs; every site a curative sanctuary at thermal or mineral waters.
claims.statement_id: Dewi Galia (Gaulish) mata air penyembuh; setiap situs tempat suci air panas atau mineral.
claims.quote: Damona belongs to the group of Gaulish goddesses of the healing springs. At every site where she is named the setting is a curative sanctuary attached to thermal or mineral waters.

claims.statement: Per Miranda Aldhouse-Green, Alesia was her main sanctuary with Apollo Moritasgus; a statue fragment: head crowned with ears of corn.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Miranda Aldhouse-Green (Alhouse-Green), Alesia tempat suci utama bersama Apollo Moritasgus; pecahan arca: kepala bermahkota bulir gandum.
claims.quote: Alhouse-Green regards Alesia as Damona's principal sanctuary, where she was worshipped with Apollo Moritasgus at a precinct that enclosed sacred springs and baths in which the sick bathed in hope of a cure. No image of Moritasgus survives, but a fragment of Damona's cult statue was recovered there: a carved stone head crowned with ears of corn

claims.statement: Damona is a Celtic goddess (keltischen Göttin), partner of the healing god Bormo (Borvo), so also called Bormana.
claims.statement_id: Damona dewi Kelt (keltischen Göttin), pasangan dewa penyembuh Bormo (Borvo), juga disebut Bormana.
claims.quote: Damona ist der Name einer keltischen Göttin. Sie ist die Partnerin des Heilgottes Bormo, als solche auch Bormana genannt.

claims.statement: Birkhan: a spring nymph (Quellnymphe) worshipped as a hind (Hindengestalt).
claims.statement_id: Birkhan: nimfa mata air (Quellnymphe) yang dipuja dalam wujud rusa betina (Hindengestalt).
claims.quote: Birkhan nimmt an, dass sie eine Quellnymphe war und nicht in Rinder-, sondern in Hindengestalt verehrt wurde.

claims.statement: Worshipped at Aquae Bormonis (Bourbon-Lancy) and Bourbonne-les-Bains.
claims.statement_id: Dipuja di Aquae Bormonis (Bourbon-Lancy) dan Bourbonne-les-Bains.
claims.quote: Damona wurde in den Orten Aquae Bormonis (Bourbon-Lancy, Département Saône-et-Loire, römischen Provinz Lugdunensis) im Gebiet der Häduer und Bourbonne-les-Bains

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Objek, bukan makhluk: Double-headed serpent adalah patung mosaik pirus Aztek (abad ke-15/16) yang disimpan di British Museum; artikelnya membahas bahan, pembuatan, dan asal-usul benda itu, bukan sosok makhluk mitologi. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-headed_serpent).

claims.statement: In English folklore the Grindylow (Grundylow) is a creature of Yorkshire and Lancashire; its name is linked to Grendel (Beowulf, Old English).
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Grindylow (Grundylow) makhluk Yorkshire dan Lancashire; nama terkait Grendel (Beowulf, Inggris Kuno/Old English); di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: In English folklore, Grindylow or Grundylow is a creature in the counties of Yorkshire and Lancashire. The name is thought to be connected to Grendel, a name or term used in Beowulf and in many Old English charters where it is seen in connection with meres, bogs and lakes.

claims.statement: Tiny scaly greenish humanoids with sharp claws and teeth and long arms; especially Lancaster.
claims.statement_id: Humanoid kecil bersisik, kehijauan, cakar dan gigi tajam, lengan panjang; terutama Lancaster.
claims.quote: Grindylows are supernatural creatures that appear in the folklore of England, most notably the Lancaster area. They are described as diminutive humanoids with scaly skin, a greenish complexion, sharp claws and teeth, and long, wiry arms with lengthy fingers at the end.

claims.statement: They dwell in ponds and marshes, seizing children with a strong grip and dragging them under.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di kolam dan rawa, menangkap anak dengan cengkeraman kuat dan menyeretnya ke air.
claims.quote: They are said to dwell in ponds and marshes waiting for unsuspecting children, which they grab with their shockingly strong grip, and then drag under the surface of the waters.

claims.statement: Used to frighten children; similar spirits Peg Powler, Nelly Longarms, Jenny Greenteeth.
claims.statement_id: Dipakai menakuti anak; roh serupa Peg Powler, Nelly Longarms, Jenny Greenteeth.
claims.quote: Grindylows have been used as shadowy figures to frighten children away from pools, marshes, or ponds where they could drown. Peg Powler, Nelly Longarms, and Jenny Greenteeth are similar water spirits.

claims.statement: The grindylow (grundylow) is a folk creature of England (Angleterre), Yorkshire and Lancashire, grabbing children with long arms to the bottom of lakes.
claims.statement_id: Grindylow (grundylow) makhluk folklore Inggris (Angleterre), Yorkshire dan Lancashire, menangkap anak dengan lengan panjang ke dasar danau.
claims.quote: Un grindylow ou grundylow est une créature folklorique originaire d'Angleterre, aux alentours des comtés de Yorkshire et Lancashire. Il a pour habitude d'attraper les enfants grâce à ses longs bras et de les emmener au fond des lacs et mares où il réside.

claims.statement: A Grindylow puppet based on English (anglais) folklore was made for the Harry Potter films (Univers de Harry Potter).
claims.statement_id: Boneka Grindylow dari folklore Inggris (anglais) dibuat untuk film Harry Potter (Univers de Harry Potter).
claims.quote: Grindylow Marionnette basée sur Grindylow du folklore anglais, développée pour la série de films de fantasy de l'Univers de Harry Potter

claims.statement: Lludd Llaw Ereint (Lludd of the Silver Hand), son of Beli Mawr, is a Welsh hero; as Nudd Llaw Ereint, cognate with the Irish Nuada Airgetlám, from the Celtic god Nodens; father of Gwyn ap Nudd; source of King Lud in Geoffrey of Monmouth's History of the Kings of Britain.
claims.statement_id: Lludd Llaw Ereint (Lludd of the Silver Hand), putra Beli Mawr, pahlawan mitologi Wales (Welsh); Nudd Llaw Ereint sekerabat Nuada Airgetlám Irlandia (Irish), dari dewa Kelt (Celtic) pra-Romawi Nodens; ayah Gwyn ap Nudd; sumber raja Lud dalam History of the Kings of Britain (Geoffrey of Monmouth); di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Lludd Llaw Ereint ("Lludd of the Silver Hand") son of Beli Mawr, is a legendary hero from Welsh mythology. As Nudd Llaw Ereint (the earlier form of his name, cognate of the Irish Nuada Airgetlám, derived from the pre-Roman Celtic god Nodens) he is the father of Gwyn ap Nudd. He is probably the source of king Lud from Geoffrey of Monmouth's History of the Kings of Britain.

claims.statement: In the Mabinogion tale Lludd and Llefelys, Lludd rules Britain, Llefelys Gaul; three plagues.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mabinogion, Lludd and Llefelys: Lludd penguasa Britania (Britain), Llefelys di Galia (Gaul); tiga wabah.
claims.quote: In the Mabinogion tale of Lludd and Llefelys, which influenced Geoffrey of Monmouth's work, he is the ruler of Britain while his brother Llefelys ruled Gaul. Lludd calls on Llefelys to rid Britain of three plagues then afflicting the kingdom.

claims.statement: The first plague: the Coranians, dwarfs from Asia, perhaps the Romans.
claims.statement_id: Wabah pertama Coranians, kerdil dari Asia (Asia), mungkin bangsa Romawi (Romans).
claims.quote: The first plague was that of the Coranians a race of dwarfs 'from Asia' who may represent the Romans.

claims.statement: The second: white and red dragons (Brythons and Anglo-Saxons), fighting on May Day eve.
claims.statement_id: Wabah kedua naga putih dan merah (Brythons, Briton; Anglo-Saxon), bertarung malam May Day.
claims.quote: The second was that of the white and red dragons. One of the dragons represented the Brythons, while the other represented the Anglo-Saxon invaders of Britain. On the eve of May Day, the two dragons would begin to fight.

claims.statement: The dragons were buried in a rock pit at Dinas Emrys, Snowdonia.
claims.statement_id: Naga dikubur di lubang batu di Dinas Emrys, Snowdonia.
claims.quote: The plague was finally eradicated by catching the dragons and burying both of them in a rock pit at Dinas Emrys in Snowdonia, north Wales, the securest place in Britain at that time.

claims.statement: Lludd is the legendary founder (sagenhafte Gründer) of London (Londons; Caer Lludd, Llundain).
claims.statement_id: Lludd pendiri legendaris (sagenhafte Gründer) London (Londons; Caer Lludd, Llundain).
claims.quote: Er gilt als der sagenhafte Gründer Londons (Caer Lludd, Llundain).

claims.statement: His daughter Creiddylad was the model for Shakespeare's (Shakespeares) Cordelia.
claims.statement_id: Putrinya Creiddylad teladan Cordelia karya Shakespeare (Shakespeares).
claims.quote: Lludd Llawereint hat in der Erzählung Mal y kavas Kulhwch Olwen („Wie Kulhwch Olwen errungen hat“) Creiddylad zur Tochter, das Vorbild für Shakespeares Cordelia

claims.statement: Ludgate in London is named after Lludd; near St Paul's Cathedral.
claims.statement_id: Ludgate di London dinamai menurut Lludd; dekat St Paul's Cathedral.
claims.quote: Philological connection suggests that there was once a memorial to Lludd at the site of St Paul's Cathedral, London, near Ludgate, which is named after him.

claims.statement: The dragons were caught at Oxford, the exact centre of Britain.
claims.statement_id: Naga ditangkap di Oxford, pusat pulau Britania (Britain).
claims.quote: This place was at Oxford, which Lludd found to be the exact centre of the island when he measured the island of Britain.

claims.statement: The merrow (Irish murúch; Middle Irish murdúchann) is a mermaid or merman of Irish folklore needing a magic cap (cochaillín draíochta, cohuleen druith).
claims.statement_id: Merrow (Irlandia/Irish murúch; Irlandia Pertengahan/Middle Irish murdúchann) duyung cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore), perlu topi ajaib (cochaillín draíochta, cohuleen druith); di Irlandia.
claims.quote: Merrow (from Irish murúch , Middle Irish murdúchann or murdúchu ) is a mermaid or merman in Irish folklore. The term is anglicised from the Irish word murúch. The merrows supposedly require a magical cap (Irish: cochaillín draíochta ; anglicised: cohuleen druith) in order to travel between deep water and dry land.

claims.statement: Lady of Gollerus: a green-haired merrow weds a Kerry man who takes her red cap; The Soul Cages: a green male merrow; 19th-century Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Lady of Gollerus: merrow berambut hijau menikah dengan lelaki Kerry yang mengambil topi merahnya; The Soul Cages: merrow lelaki hijau; Irlandia (Ireland) abad ke-19.
claims.quote: "Lady of Gollerus", where a green-haired merrow weds a local Kerry man who deprives her of the "magical red cap" (cohuleen druith ); and "The Soul Cages" where a green-bodied grotesque male merrow entertains a fisherman at his home under the sea.

claims.statement: Published in T. C. Croker's Fairy Legends (1828); W. B. Yeats borrowed; The Soul Cages was fiction by Thomas Keightley.
claims.statement_id: Terbit dalam Fairy Legends (1828) T. C. Croker; W. B. Yeats (William Butler Yeats) meminjam; The Soul Cages rekaan Thomas Keightley.
claims.quote: These tales with commentary were first published in T. C. Croker's Fairy Legends (1828). William Butler Yeats and others writing on the subject borrowed heavily from this work. "The Soul Cages" turned out not to be a genuine folktale, but rather a piece of fiction fabricated by Thomas Keightley.

claims.statement: Merrow is a Hiberno-English term from murúch, sea singer or siren.
claims.statement_id: Merrow istilah Hiberno-Inggris (Hiberno-English) dari murúch, penyanyi laut atau siren.
claims.quote: Current scholarship regards merrow as a Hiberno-English term, derived from Irish murúch (Middle Irish murdhúchu or murdúchann ) meaning "sea singer" or "siren".

claims.statement: In Scots dialect, morrough.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dialek Skotlandia (Scots) morrough.
claims.quote: The corresponding term in the Scots dialect is morrough , derived from the Irish, with no original Scottish Gaelic form suggested.

claims.statement: The merrow (Murrough) is the Scottish and Irish (schottische und irische) equivalent of mermaids (Meerjungfrauen); human to the waist, fish below.
claims.statement_id: Merrow (Murrough) padanan Skotlandia dan Irlandia (schottische und irische) bagi putri duyung (Meerjungfrauen, Mermaid); manusia hingga pinggang, ikan di bawah.
claims.quote: Merrow (aus dem gälischen murúch) oder Murrough (Galloway) ist ein Meermann und das schottische und irische Äquivalent zu den Meerjungfrauen anderer Kulturen. Über diese Wesen wird gesagt, dass sie vom Kopf bis zur Taille menschlich seien, von der Taille abwärts hätten sie den Körper eines Fisches.

claims.statement: They have a friendly, modest, loving and kindly nature.
claims.statement_id: Berwatak ramah, sederhana, penyayang, dan baik hati.
claims.quote: Sie haben eine freundliche, bescheidene, liebevolle und wohlwollende Veranlagung.

claims.statement: Ritona (Pritona; Gaulish she of the ford) was a Celtic goddess of Roman Gaul among the Treveri of the Moselle; a goddess of fords; temple at Augusta Treverorum (Trier), Altbach.
claims.statement_id: Ritona (Pritona; Galia, Gaulish: dia dari arungan) dewi Kelt (Celtic) Galia Romawi (Roman Gaul), suku Treveri, Moselle; dewi arungan; kuil di Augusta Treverorum (Trier), Altbach; di Jerman dan Prancis.
claims.quote: Gaulish for 'she of the ford') was an ancient Celtic goddess worshipped in Roman Gaul, above all among the Treveri of the Moselle. She is generally interpreted as a goddess of fords and river crossings. Her chief cult lay at Augusta Treverorum (modern Trier), where she had a temple in the Altbach valley sanctuary.

claims.statement: The name is from the Gaulish word for ford; two forms Ritona and Pritona.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari kata Galia (Gaulish) untuk arungan; dua bentuk Ritona dan Pritona.
claims.quote: Her name is built on the Gaulish word for 'ford' and occurs in two variant forms, Ritona and Pritona.

claims.statement: ritu- survives in Welsh rhyd, Cornish rid and Breton rit (ford).
claims.statement_id: ritu- bertahan dalam Wales (Welsh) rhyd, Cornwall (Cornish) rid, Breton rit (arungan).
claims.quote: The inherited initial p was lost, as regularly in Celtic, and the reflex ritu- survives in Welsh rhyd, Cornish rid and Breton rit ('ford').

claims.statement: A group of Treveran water and spring deities such as Icovellauna.
claims.statement_id: Kelompok dewa air dan mata air Treveri (Treveran) seperti Icovellauna.
claims.quote: Ritona belongs to a group of Treveran deities of water and springs known chiefly from inscriptions, among them Icovellauna, who was honoured at Trier and at Metz.

claims.statement: Ritona (Pritona) was a Celtic goddess (keltische Göttin) with temples at Contiomagus (Pachten) and the Altbachtal, Trier; a dedication at Uzès in southern France (südfranzösischen).
claims.statement_id: Ritona (Pritona) dewi Kelt (keltische Göttin), kuil di Contiomagus (Pachten) dan Altbachtal, Trier; prasasti di Uzès, Prancis selatan (südfranzösischen).
claims.quote: Ritona, auch Pritona war eine keltische Göttin, der im vicus Contiomagus (Pachten, Ortsteil von Dillingen/Saar) und im Tempelbezirk im Altbachtal in Augusta Treverorum (Trier) ein Tempel gewidmet war. Aber auch im südfranzösischen Uzès wurde eine Weiheinschrift für sie gefunden.

claims.statement: Protective goddess (Schutzgöttin) of the watercourse and ford (Furt) across the Saar at Contiomagus.
claims.statement_id: Dewi pelindung (Schutzgöttin) aliran air dan arungan (Furt) Sungai Saar di Contiomagus.
claims.quote: Ritona war eine Schutzgöttin des Wasserlaufes und der Furt (-ritum „Furt“) durch die Saar bei Contiomagus.

claims.statement: Paul-Marie Duval and Lothar Schwinden: Pritona is the earlier form.
claims.statement_id: Paul-Marie Duval dan Lothar Schwinden: Pritona bentuk lebih tua.
claims.quote: Paul-Marie Duval and Lothar Schwinden take Pritona to be the earlier form, keeping the initial p- of the archaic name.

claims.statement: Also attested at Contiomagus (Pachten, Saar) and southern Gaul.
claims.statement_id: Juga tercatat di Contiomagus (Pachten, Saar) dan Galia selatan.
claims.quote: She is also attested at the village of Contiomagus (modern Pachten, Saar) and in southern Gaul.

claims.statement: Tarvos Trigaranus (Taruos Trigaranos) is a divine figure on a Pillar of the Boatmen relief, a bull with three cranes.
claims.statement_id: Tarvos Trigaranus (Taruos Trigaranos) sosok ilahi pada relief Pillar of the Boatmen, banteng dengan tiga bangau; di Prancis.
claims.quote: Tarvos Trigaranus or Taruos Trigaranos is a divine figure who appears on a relief panel of the Pillar of the Boatmen as a bull with three cranes perched on his back.

claims.statement: On the next panel the god Esus chops a tree with an axe.
claims.statement_id: Di panel sebelah, dewa Esus menebang pohon dengan kapak.
claims.quote: He stands under a tree, and on an adjacent panel, the god Esus is chopping down a tree, possibly a willow, with an axe.

claims.statement: Gaulish taruos bull; Old Irish tarb; Welsh tarw; garanus crane, tri- three.
claims.statement_id: Galia (Gaulish) taruos banteng; Irlandia Kuno (Old Irish) tarb; Wales (Welsh) tarw; garanus bangau, tri- tiga.
claims.quote: In the Gaulish language, taruos means "bull," found in Old Irish as tarb (/tarβ/), in Modern Irish/Gaelic as tarbh and in Welsh as tarw

claims.statement: A pillar from Trier: a man with an axe fells a tree with three birds and a bull's head.
claims.statement_id: Pilar dari Trier: lelaki berkapak menebang pohon dengan tiga burung dan kepala banteng.
claims.quote: A pillar from Trier shows a man with an axe cutting down a tree in which sit three birds and a bull's head.

claims.statement: Tarvos Trigaranus, the bull with three cranes (Stier mit den drei Kranichen), is a Celtic deity (keltische Gottheit).
claims.statement_id: Tarvos Trigaranus, banteng dengan tiga bangau (Stier mit den drei Kranichen), dewa Kelt (keltische Gottheit).
claims.quote: Der Tarvos Trigaranus („Stier mit den drei Kranichen“) ist eine keltische Gottheit.

claims.statement: The name is known from one inscription (Inschrift), on the pillar of the Nautae Parisiaci; no mythology is known. (Paris)
claims.statement_id: Nama hanya dari satu prasasti (Inschrift), di pilar Nautae Parisiaci; tak ada mitologi diketahui. (Paris)
claims.quote: Der Name ist einzig aus einer Inschrift bekannt, irgendeine Mythologie dazu ist nicht bekannt.

claims.statement: A Tarvos and Esus myth is suspected but unproven.
claims.statement_id: Mitos Tarvos dan Esus diduga, belum terbukti.
claims.quote: Ob es einen Mythos mit Tarvos und Esus gibt, wird vermutet, ist aber derzeit nicht belegbar.

claims.statement: At the Gallo-Roman (galloromanischen) temple of Maiden Castle a bronze statuette of a bull was found.
claims.statement_id: Di kuil Galia-Romawi (galloromanischen) Maiden Castle ditemukan patung perunggu kecil banteng.
claims.quote: Im galloromanischen Tempel von Maiden Castle wurde eine Bronzestatuette gefunden, die einen Stier und drei mi

claims.statement: Black Shuck tales belong to the folklore of Norfolk, Suffolk, the Cambridgeshire Fens and Essex; sometimes an omen of death, sometimes companionable.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Black Shuck bagian dari cerita rakyat Norfolk, Suffolk, Cambridgeshire Fens, Essex (East Anglia); kadang pertanda kematian, kadang teman; anjing hitam (Black dog), Old Shuck, Old Shock; Inggris (English folklore), Kepulauan Britania (British Isles); di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: Accounts of Black Shuck form part of the folklore of Norfolk, Suffolk, the Cambridgeshire Fens and Essex, and descriptions of the creature's appearance and nature vary considerably; it is sometimes recorded as an omen of death, but, in other instances, is described as companionable.

claims.statement: Per the Oxford English Dictionary, from Old English scucca, devil, fiend.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Oxford English Dictionary dari Inggris Kuno (Old English) scucca, setan; Norfolk, Suffolk, Cambridgeshire Fens, Essex.
claims.quote: According to the Oxford English Dictionary, the name Shuck derives from the Old English word scucca 'devil, fiend', perhaps from the root skuh 'to terrify'.

claims.statement: First printed mention by Reverend E. S. Taylor in Notes and Queries, 1850: a shaggy fiery-eyed dog visiting churchyards at midnight.
claims.statement_id: Penyebutan tertulis pertama oleh Pendeta (Reverend) E. S. Taylor, Notes and Queries 1850: anjing hitam berbulu, bermata api, mengunjungi pekuburan tengah malam.
claims.quote: The first mention in print of "Black Shuck" is by Reverend E. S. Taylor in an 1850 edition of the journal Notes and Queries which describes "Shuck the Dog-fiend"

claims.statement: Abraham Fleming's account of its 1577 appearance at Bungay, Suffolk.
claims.statement_id: Catatan Abraham Fleming tentang kemunculan di Bungay, Suffolk, 1577.
claims.quote: Abraham Fleming's account of the appearance of A strange, and terrible wunder in 1577 at Bungay, Suffolk is a famous account of the beast.

claims.statement: W. A. Dutt (1901): one fiery eye in the middle of his head like a Cyclops; meeting him warns of death within the year.
claims.statement_id: W. A. Dutt (1901): satu mata api di tengah kepala seperti Cyclops; bertemu dengannya pertanda mati sebelum akhir tahun.
claims.quote: You may know him at once, should you see him, by his fiery eye; he has but one, and that, like the Cyclops', is in the middle of his head. But such an encounter might bring you the worst of luck: it is even said that to meet him is to be warned that your death will occur before the end of the year.

claims.statement: The legend probably inspired Arthur Conan Doyle's Der Hund von Baskerville (The Hound of the Baskervilles).
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini kemungkinan mengilhami Arthur Conan Doyle menulis Der Hund von Baskerville (The Hound of the Baskervilles).
claims.quote: Sehr wahrscheinlich ist, dass die Sage Arthur Conan Doyle Anreiz dazu gab, den Sherlock-Holmes-Roman Der Hund von Baskerville zu verfassen.

claims.statement: Black Shuck (der Alte Shuck) is a mysterious black ghost dog (schwarzen Geisterhundes) said to haunt Norfolk, Essex and Suffolk.
claims.statement_id: Black Shuck (der Alte Shuck) anjing hantu hitam (schwarzen Geisterhundes) yang menghantui Norfolk, Essex, Suffolk.
claims.quote: Black Shuck oder der Alte Shuck ist der Name eines geheimnisumwobenen schwarzen Geisterhundes, der angeblich in Norfolk, Essex und Suffolk spuken soll.

claims.statement: The boobrie is a shapeshifter of west-coast Scottish lochs, a giant water bird like a cormorant or great northern diver, or a water bull.
claims.statement_id: Boobrie pengubah wujud di danau (lochs) pantai barat Skotlandia (Scotland), burung air raksasa mirip kormoran atau great northern diver, juga banteng air; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: The boobrie is a mythological shapeshifting entity inhabiting the lochs of the west coast of Scotland. It commonly adopts the appearance of a gigantic water bird resembling a cormorant or great northern diver, but it can also materialise in the form of various other mythological creatures such as a water bull.

claims.statement: As a water horse it gallops over lochs; in summer an insect sucking horses' blood.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai kuda air berlari di atas danau; pada musim panas serangga pengisap darah kuda.
claims.quote: In its manifestation as a water horse the creature is able to gallop across the top of lochs as if on solid ground. During the summer months it is seen infrequently as a large insect, sucking the blood of horses.

claims.statement: Edward Dwelly: tarbh-boidhre, monster, demon, god capable of many forms.
claims.statement_id: Edward Dwelly: tarbh-boidhre monster, iblis, dewa yang dapat berubah banyak wujud.
claims.quote: Edward Dwelly, a Scottish lexicographer, lists tarbh-boidhre as "Monster, demon" and "God capable of changing himself into many forms"

claims.statement: Campbell of Islay: based on the great auk; its call from the bittern.
claims.statement_id: Campbell of Islay: dari great auk; suaranya dari burung bittern.
claims.quote: Folklorist Campbell of Islay has speculated that descriptions of the boobrie may be based on sightings of the great auk. The bellowing sound made by the boobrie, more like a bull than a bird, may have its origin in the strange call of the common bittern

claims.statement: Boobrie may derive from boibhre, cow giver.
claims.statement_id: Boobrie mungkin dari boibhre, pemberi sapi.
claims.quote: Boobrie may derive from boibhre , meaning cow giver or cow bestowing.

claims.statement: A huge seabird like the cormorant or Plongeon huard, white-spotted, bellowing, devouring sheep and cattle.
claims.statement_id: Burung laut raksasa mirip kormoran atau Plongeon huard, berbintik putih, melenguh, melahap domba dan sapi.
claims.quote: Il est communément décrit comme un énorme oiseau de mer, ressemblant au cormoran ou au Plongeon huard (Gavia immer), mais dont le corps serait taché de blanc et qui serait capable de mugir. Sa corpulence lui permet de dévorer des moutons et des bovins.

claims.statement: A transformed shape of the Each Uisge, an evil horse haunting loch shores.
claims.statement_id: Wujud jelmaan Each Uisge (Each-uisge), kuda jahat di tepi danau.
claims.quote: Cette créature est censée hanter les lacs et les puits de sel et serait la forme métamorphosée du Each Uisge, cheval maléfique hantant les rivages des lochs.

claims.statement: It preys on animals carried on ships, mainly calves; very fond of otters.
claims.statement_id: Memangsa ternak di kapal, terutama anak sapi; sangat gemar berang-berang.
claims.quote: It commonly preys on animals being transported on ships, preferably calves, but will also happily eat lambs and sheep, carrying its prey away to the deepest water before consuming it. It is also extremely fond of otters, which it consumes in large quantities.

claims.statement: The Bugul Noz (Night Shepherd) is a nocturnal fairy of Breton folklore from Morbihan, Brittany.
claims.statement_id: Bugul Noz (Gembala Malam, Night Shepherd) peri malam cerita rakyat Breton (Breton folklore), Morbihan, Brittany; di Prancis.
claims.quote: The Bugul Noz ([byɡylˈnoːs] "Night Shepherd" or "child of the night") is a nocturnal fairy or bogeyman-like being in Breton folklore, from Morbihan, Brittany.

claims.statement: Émilie Carpentier: a small clawed man with fiery eyes and whistling voice; avoids the cross; drowns captives at cockcrow.
claims.statement_id: Émilie Carpentier: lelaki kecil bercakar, mata api, suara bersiul; menghindari salib; menenggelamkan tawanan saat ayam berkokok.
claims.quote: Émilie Carpentier described the Bugul-Noz as a little man with claws, fiery eyes, and a whistling voice, who threatened shepherds and workers who linger outside after dark. In one story, the "bugul noz" rides at night, although he turns back at the sight of crossroads to avoid the shape of the cross. If he takes a person prisoner, he will drown them as soon as the cock crows.

claims.statement: Anatole Le Braz: a tall figure at twilight; an informant: a benevolent spirit.
claims.statement_id: Anatole Le Braz (French Literature): sosok tinggi saat senja; narasumber: roh baik.
claims.quote: Anatole Le Braz, a professor of French Literature, heard of the Bugul-Noz as a tall, foreboding figure who appears at twilight. One informant suggested that rather than a threatening figure, the Bugul-Noz was a benevolent spirit influencing people not to linger outside where it was not safe after dark.

claims.statement: An animal pelt for a wolf-like form, big hat and cloak; grows as it nears victims.
claims.statement_id: Kulit binatang untuk wujud serigala, topi besar dan jubah; membesar saat mendekati korban.
claims.quote: The Bugul-Noz has also been described as having an animal pelt that allows it to take a wolf-like form and wearing a large hat and cloak. In this version, the Bugul-Noz grows larger as he approaches his victims.

claims.statement: From bugel (child, shepherd; Kind, Hirte) and noz (night, Nacht); appears in woods (Wäldern) and lonely paths.
claims.statement_id: Nama dari bugel (anak, gembala; Kind, Hirte) dan noz (malam, Nacht); muncul di hutan (Wäldern) dan jalan sepi.
claims.quote: Der Name leitet sich ab von bugel (Kind, Knabe, auch Hirte) und noz (Nacht) und bezeichnet eine nächtliche Kreatur oder einen Geist, der bevorzugt in Wäldern und auf einsamen Wegen erscheint.

claims.statement: Tales from southern Brittany (Bretagne), the Pays Vannetais.
claims.statement_id: Kisah dari Brittany selatan (Bretagne), Pays Vannetais.
claims.quote: Die Geschichten um den Bugul-Noz stammen insbesondere aus dem südlichen Teil der Bretagne, etwa dem Pays Vannetais.

claims.statement: The church grim is a guardian spirit of Scottish, English and Nordic folklore protecting a Christian church and its churchyard, often a black dog.
claims.statement_id: Church grim roh penjaga dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish), Inggris (English), Nordik (Nordic), menjaga gereja Kristen (Christian) dan pekuburan; sering anjing hitam; di Britania, Swedia, Denmark.
claims.quote: The church grim is a guardian spirit in Scottish, English and Nordic folklore that oversees the welfare of a particular Christian church, and protects the churchyard from those who would profane and commit sacrilege against it. It often appears as a black dog but is known to take the form of other animals.

claims.statement: The English grim is a big red-eyed black dog guarding churchyards against thieves, witches and the Devil.
claims.statement_id: Grim Inggris (English) anjing hitam besar bermata merah, menjaga pekuburan dari pencuri, penyihir, Iblis (Devil).
claims.quote: The English church grim usually takes the form of a large black dog with red eyes and guards churchyards from those who would profane them, including thieves, vandals, witches, warlocks, and the Devil himself.

claims.statement: Yorkshire tradition: the grim tolls the bell at midnight before a death; like many spectral black dogs.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi Yorkshire: grim membunyikan lonceng tengah malam sebelum kematian; seperti banyak anjing hitam hantu.
claims.quote: Like many spectral black dogs, the grim, according to Yorkshire tradition, is also an ominous warning and is known to toll the church bell at midnight before a death takes place.

claims.statement: In Scotland the spirit of the latest buried guarded the churchyard; the faire chlaidh.
claims.statement_id: Di Skotlandia (Scotland), arwah orang terakhir dikubur menjaga pekuburan; faire chlaidh.
claims.quote: According to a related belief in Scotland, the spirit of the person most recently buried in a churchyard had to protect it until the next funeral provided a new guardian to replace them. This churchyard vigil was known as the faire chlaidh

claims.statement: The Scandinavian grim, Kyrkogrim (Swedish), Kirkonväki (Finnish), Kirkegrim (Danish), is the revenant of an animal buried alive in the foundation.
claims.statement_id: Grim Skandinavia (Scandinavian): Kyrkogrim (Swedish, Swedia), Kirkonväki (Finnish, Finlandia), Kirkegrim (Danish, Denmark), arwah hewan dikubur hidup di fondasi gereja.
claims.quote: The Scandinavian church grim is also known as the Kyrkogrim (Swedish), Kirkonväki (Finnish), and Kirkegrim (Danish) is likewise defined as the protective revenant of an animal buried alive in the church foundation.

claims.statement: English (Английские) grims love bell-ringing; they appear as black dogs or small dark disproportionate people.
claims.statement_id: Grim Inggris (Английские) suka dentang lonceng; muncul sebagai anjing hitam atau orang kecil gelap berbentuk tak seimbang.
claims.quote: Английские церковные гримы любят слушать колокольный звон. Могут являться в виде чёрных собак или в виде маленьких, непропорционально сложенных темнокожих человечков.

claims.statement: 19th-century folklorists believed a dog was buried alive under the cornerstone as a foundation sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Abad ke-19: folklorist percaya anjing dikubur hidup di bawah batu penjuru sebagai kurban fondasi.
claims.quote: In the 19th century, folklorists believed that it had once been the custom to bury a dog alive under the cornerstone of a church as a foundation sacrifice so that its ghost might serve as a guardian.

claims.statement: The cù-sìth (coin-shìth) is a mythical hound of Irish and Scottish folklore, cú sídhe; like the Welsh Cŵn Annwn.
claims.statement_id: Cù-sìth (coin-shìth) anjing mitos cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish folklore) dan Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), cú sídhe; mirip Cŵn Annwn Wales (Welsh); di Britania dan Irlandia.
claims.quote: is a mythical hound found in Irish folklore and Scottish folklore. In Irish folklore it is spelled cú sídhe, and it also bears some resemblance to the Welsh Cŵn Annwn.

claims.statement: Lives in rock clefts and roams the Highland moors; dark green shaggy coat; size of a small cow.
claims.statement_id: Tinggal di celah batu, menjelajahi padang Dataran Tinggi (Highlands); bulu hijau gelap; seukuran sapi kecil.
claims.quote: The cù-sìth is thought to make its home in the clefts of rocks and to roam the moors of the Highlands. It is usually described as having a shaggy, dark green coat with deeper green fur on the ears and more yellow fur towards the feet. It is said to be the size of a small cow

claims.statement: More dangerous than the Cat-Sith, taking souls of the living.
claims.statement_id: Lebih berbahaya daripada Cat-Sith (Cat-sìth), mengambil jiwa orang hidup.
claims.quote: The Cù-Sìth was considered to be more dangerous than the similar Cat-Sith, as it was able to take the souls of the living as opposed to just those of the dead.

claims.statement: Hunts silently; three terrifying barks; one must reach safety by the third.
claims.statement_id: Berburu diam-diam, tiga gonggongan mengerikan; harus aman sebelum gonggongan ketiga.
claims.quote: According to legend, the creature was capable of hunting silently, but would occasionally let out three terrifying barks, and only three, that could be heard for miles by those listening for it, even far out at sea. Those who hear the barking of the Cù-Sìth must reach safety by the third bark or be overcome with terror to the point of death.

claims.statement: Coin-shìth served the Fae Folk as watchdogs.
claims.statement_id: Coin-shìth dipakai para peri (Fae Folk) sebagai anjing penjaga.
claims.quote: When Coin-shìth weren't hunting, they were used by the Fae Folk as watchdogs or as expedition companions.

claims.statement: The Cu Sith hunts silently and creeps up from behind to steal souls (Seelen).
claims.statement_id: Cu Sith berburu tanpa suara dan menyelinap dari belakang untuk mencuri jiwa (Seelen).
claims.quote: Das Wesen jagt lautlos und schleicht sich von hinten an Opfer heran um ihre Seelen zu entführen.

claims.statement: Nursing women were more at risk, kidnapped to nurse fairy children.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan menyusui lebih rentan, diculik untuk menyusui anak peri.
claims.quote: Women who were breastfeeding were considered more vulnerable to attacks of the Cù-Sìth, as it was believed that the it would kidnap the them and force them to nurse faerie children.

claims.statement: Enbarr (Énbarr, Aonbharr; Irish Aonbharr Mhanannáin) is a horse of the Irish Mythological Cycle crossing land and sea; owned by Manannan mac Lir, used by Lugh Lamh-fada; Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann; Sguaba Tuinne.
claims.statement_id: Enbarr (Énbarr, Aonbharr; Irlandia/Irish Aonbharr Mhanannáin) kuda Siklus Mitologi Irlandia, melintasi darat dan laut; milik Manannan mac Lir (Manannán mac Lir), dipakai Lugh Lamh-fada; Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann; Sguaba Tuinne; di Irlandia.
claims.quote: is a horse in the Irish Mythological Cycle which could traverse both land and sea, swifter than wind-speed. The horse was the property of the sea-god Manannan mac Lir, but provided to Lugh Lamh-fada (Irish: Luġ Lámhfhada ) to use at his disposal. In the story Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann ("The Fate of the Children of Tuireann"), Lugh refused to lend it to the sons of Tuireann

claims.statement: Cormac's glossary: froth; O'Curry: One Mane; James Mackillop: unique supremacy.
claims.statement_id: Cormac's glossary: buih (froth); O'Curry: Satu Surai (One Mane); James Mackillop: supremasi unik.
claims.quote: As a common noun enbarr is defined as "froth" in the medieval Cormac's glossary. The modern Irish form Aonbharr is glossed as "One Mane" by O'Curry

claims.statement: Quicker than the cold wind of spring; its rider could not be killed.
claims.statement_id: Lebih cepat dari angin dingin musim semi; penunggangnya tak dapat dibunuh.
claims.quote: The horse was quicker than the "naked cold wind of spring", and could travel over land or sea with equal ease. It also had the property that whoever was mounted on its back could not be killed.

claims.statement: Enbarr Manannán (Aenbharr, Aonbharr, Énbarr) is Lugh Lamh-fada's horse in the Irish Mythological Cycle.
claims.statement_id: Enbarr Manannán (Aenbharr, Aonbharr, Énbarr) kuda Lugh Lamh-fada dalam Siklus Mitologi Irlandia (Irlandia Klasik).
claims.quote: Enbarr Manannán, atau Enbarr dengan surai menjuntai, (juga ditulis Aenbharr, Aonbharr, Aonbárr, Énbarr, Enbhárr; Irlandia Klasik: Aonḃaɼɼ Mhanannáin) adalah nama dalam Siklus Mitologi Irlandia dari kuda Lugh Lamh-fada

claims.statement: Embarr was taken as Niamh's horse carrying Oisín and Niamh to Tír na nÓg (Mícheál Coimín).
claims.statement_id: Embarr dianggap kuda Niamh yang membawa Oisín dan Niamh ke Tír na nÓg (Mícheál Coimín).
claims.quote: Nama Embarr ("imajinasi") tampaknya telah dianggap sebagai kuda Niamh. Kuda khusus membawa Oisín dan calon pengantinnya Niamh menyebrangi laut menuju Tír na nÓg, menurut Laoi Oisín as ṫír na n-óg (tibanya Oisín di tanah muda) oleh Mícheál Coimín (1676-1760).

claims.statement: Lugh was trapped into lending the currach Besom of the Sea (scuab tuinné), also Sguaba Tuinne or Wave-sweeper.
claims.statement_id: Lugh terpaksa meminjamkan perahu currach Besom of the Sea (scuab tuinné), juga Sguaba Tuinne atau Wave-sweeper (Penyapu Ombak).
claims.quote: was later trapped into lending the self-navigating currach (coracle boat) called the "Besom of the Sea" (Irish: scuab tuinné ), also called Sguaba Tuinne or Wave-sweeper.

claims.statement: In Scottish folklore the fachan (fachin, Direach Ghlinn Eitidh) is a monster or giant described by John Francis Campbell in Popular Tales of the West Highlands: one eye, one hand from the chest, one leg.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), fachan (fachin, fachen, Direach Ghlinn Eitidh, Dithreach, kerdil Glen Etive) monster atau raksasa menurut John Francis Campbell dalam Popular Tales of the West Highlands: satu mata, satu tangan dari dada, satu kaki; di Britania Raya.
claims.quote: is a monster or giant described by John Francis Campbell in Popular Tales of the West Highlands as having a single eye in the middle of its face, a single hand protruding from its chest instead of arms, and a single leg emerging from its central axis.

claims.statement: A single tuft of hair; per Campbell easier to uproot a mountain than bend it.
claims.statement_id: Sejumput rambut; menurut Campbell lebih mudah mencabut gunung.
claims.quote: It has a single tuft of hair on the top of its head, regarding which Campbell says "it were easier to take a mountain from the root than to bend that tuft."

claims.statement: Campbell: possible Arabic influence, the nasnas or shiqq.
claims.statement_id: Campbell: kemungkinan pengaruh tradisi Arab (Arabic), nasnas (Nasnas) atau shiqq.
claims.quote: Campbell draws attention to the possible influence of creatures from Arabic tradition such as the nasnas or shiqq, described as "half of a human being" and hopping about on one leg with great agility.

claims.statement: Douglas Hyde, in his Irish folklore collection Beside the Fire, cites an Irish manuscript describing a similar monster.
claims.statement_id: Douglas Hyde, Beside the Fire (Irish folklore, Irlandia), merujuk naskah Irlandia (Irish) tentang monster serupa.
claims.quote: Douglas Hyde quotes Campbell's description in his collection of Irish folklore Beside the Fire and refers to an Irish manuscript in which a similar monster is described

claims.statement: Hyde: branches of one Gaelic tradition; fachan a diminutive of Irish fathach, giant.
claims.statement_id: Hyde: cabang tradisi Gaelik (Gaelic); fachan pengecil fathach Irlandia (Irish), raksasa.
claims.quote: Hyde suggests that both descriptions represent branches of a common Gaelic tradition, and that the word fachan may be a diminutive of the Irish fathach (giant) and related to the Scottish famhair (giant).

claims.statement: The manuscript monster: one eye in the forehead of a black face, one hand from the chest, one leg.
claims.statement_id: Monster dalam naskah: satu mata di dahi wajah hitam, satu tangan dari dada, satu kaki; lebih mirip setan.
claims.quote: and one eye in the forehead of his black-faced countenance, and one bare, hard, very hairy hand coming out of his chest, and one veiny, thick-soled leg supporting him

claims.statement: In Scottish (écossais) folklore the Fachan (Fachin, Fachen) is a monster or giant (géant) described by John Francis Campbell.
claims.statement_id: Dalam folklore Skotlandia (écossais) Fachan (Fachin, Fachen), monster atau raksasa (géant) menurut John Francis Campbell.
claims.quote: Dans le folklore écossais, le Fachan, aussi connu sous les noms de Fachin, Fachen, Direach Ghlinn Eitidh ou Dithreach (nain de Glen Etive), est un monstre ou géant décrit par John Francis Campbell dans Popular Tales of the West Highlands.
